posts.title: FSSAI Licence & Registration in 2026: The Complete Guide
posts.description: Understand the April 2026 FSSAI thresholds, activity exceptions, perpetual validity and FoSCoS application process before starting your food business.
posts.lede: A food business must identify the correct FSSAI registration or licence for its activity and premises before operating. In 2026, start with your Kind of Business, then apply the revised turnover rules; turnover alone does not settle every application.
posts.body:
What changed in FSSAI licensing in 2026?

The turnover order effective from 1 April 2026 places eligible businesses into these bands: registration up to ₹1.5 crore; State licence above ₹1.5 crore and up to ₹50 crore; Central licence above ₹50 crore. These are a starting framework. Match them to the current activity-specific eligibility row before deciding. Read the official turnover order.

The March amendment also introduced perpetual validity. It preserves annual fee and applicable return obligations, with deemed suspension for specified failures. A perpetual certificate still needs active compliance management. See amended regulation 2.1.7.

For an owner planning a new venture, these changes alter the sequence of decisions. A saved quotation, a friend's application or an old calculator may describe a different framework. Begin with today's business facts and today's official eligibility information. Keep a dated copy of the row you relied on in your application folder.

Start here: Compare registration, State licence and Central licence for the eligibility table and activity exceptions. Read the 2026 fee guide for government charges and professional-service costs.

Describe the business before choosing a licence

Write a short operational description in ordinary language. Explain what arrives at the premises, what your team does to it, what leaves, and who buys it. “We sell snacks” is incomplete if the same site also manufactures, repacks and stores them. This description is a practical planning tool, rather than a substitute for the application's formal entries.

List every location that participates in the business. Include a production kitchen, a storage site and an administrative office if relevant. Add the legal entity responsible for each location. This helps reveal situations where the brand name, leaseholder and applicant are different people or entities.

Next, map the description to the Kind of Business, often shortened to KoB. Product classification is a separate question: it concerns what the food is and which product rules apply. Resolve both questions before preparing a manufacturing application. A well-written activity description cannot repair an unsupported product classification.

For a proposed packaged-food range, collect the formulations early. Avoid deciding the route from the front label alone. A name such as “wellness drink” says little about the underlying ingredients, intended consumers or product presentation. The product-classification guide explains the difference between standardised, proprietary and non-specified routes.

Registration, State licence and Central licence: how to approach the choice

Check the official table from the top of the relevant business section. Read the complete row, including exceptions and fees. The current table identifies some activities that require a Central licence irrespective of turnover, including importing and certain specialised manufacturing activities. Use the revised KoB eligibility table.

Document the reasoning in one sentence: “The applicant carries out this activity at this premises, so this row applies.” Then record the evidence supporting any turnover declaration. This creates a useful explanation for colleagues, a consultant or a later reviewer.

If more than one activity occurs at the site, list all of them before filing. Ask whether the application reflects the full operation. If several states or legal entities are involved, create a location-and-entity map rather than treating the organisation as one undifferentiated business.

Once the route is established, scope the assistance you need. myfoodlicense.com offers registration assistance and Central licence application support. A useful engagement should explain the selected activity, the document work and the treatment of authority queries.

Prepare a consistent application file

Use an application folder with separate sections for applicant identity, business constitution, premises, activities and products. The exact upload list depends on the selected route and KoB; the document checklist explains how to assemble it without collecting every document mentioned online.

Check consistency before converting files into upload formats. The applicant's legal name should be traceable through the supporting papers. The premises description should be understandable from the address evidence. A product list should reflect the range actually proposed, with clear names rather than unexplained internal codes.

Make a small discrepancy log. For example, one document may use a shortened company name, another may show a previous address, and a landlord's document may identify a larger building than the occupied unit. Resolve the difference or prepare a truthful explanation and supporting evidence. Merely renaming the files does not solve the underlying mismatch.

Keep the original documents alongside the upload copies. Where a scan has several pages, verify that none are missing and that the signatures are readable. Avoid editing official evidence to make it appear consistent. If the evidence is wrong, correct it through the appropriate issuer or obtain the right supporting document.

Apply through the official FoSCoS portal

Use foscos.fssai.gov.in for official applications and current help material. Before entering details, have your activity assessment and document folder ready. Work through the portal's current prompts rather than relying on screenshots from an older guide.

  1. Select the location and activity. Reconcile the displayed eligibility with the route you identified from the current official table.
  2. Complete the applicant and premises information. Compare each entry with the underlying evidence before continuing.
  3. Add the relevant product information. For manufacturing activities, use the classification work prepared earlier.
  4. Upload the requested documents. Check the current file-format and size instructions shown beside each upload field.
  5. Review the declaration and payment. Read what you are declaring and save the government payment acknowledgement.
  6. Preserve the application reference. Keep the submitted version and monitor the account for further action.

These are planning stages, not a promise that every application uses identical screens or receives immediate approval. The consultant can prepare and support the application; the competent authority handles the regulatory decision.

Handle queries with an evidence-based reply

If the application is returned for clarification, read the complete query before uploading replacements. Break it into separate questions and match each one to a response and a document. This makes it easier to see whether you have actually addressed the concern.

A practical reply table contains the authority's issue, your factual explanation, the corrective action and the document filename. If the officer asks about the premises, a revised product list is unlikely to answer that question. If a formulation raises a classification problem, repeating the product's marketing name will not resolve it.

Record the deadline shown in the actual communication and portal. Do not assume that a deadline recalled from another application applies. Where the requested change affects the business itself, agree the facts internally before making declarations to the authority.

Hypothetical example

A snack brand rents a kitchen in one entity's name but starts an application under another. Its first preparation task is to establish and document the applicant's right to use the premises. The example illustrates a consistency check; it does not predict how a particular authority will decide an application.

What should you do after the certificate is issued?

Read the issued certificate against the submitted business description. Store it with the application's evidence and receipts. Share the relevant details with the team responsible for labels, procurement, operations and sales so that the approved information is used consistently.

Build an operating calendar with an owner for each task. Include the account's fee position, applicable returns, review of changes to the premises or product range, and the food-safety work relevant to the operation. The 2026 FAQ explains fee prepayment and migration arrangements; check the live account before assuming an older certificate has completed its transition. Read the implementation FAQ.

Review later amendments as well. The June 2026 licensing amendment expressly distinguishes manufacturing record requirements from non-manufacturing businesses. A generic checklist should therefore be tailored to your operation. Read the June amendment.

Finally, treat a new product, new facility or changed business model as a trigger for reassessment. Keep a change log that records what changed, who reviewed it and whether an application or other action is needed. This gives the business a workable way to maintain its regulatory position as it grows.

faq.q: Is FSSAI registration the same as a State licence?
faq.a: They are different authorisation categories. Determine the applicable category from your activity and the current official eligibility criteria; the comparison guide linked above explains the 2026 framework.

faq.q: Can I choose the cheapest category when starting a business?
faq.a: Choose the category that fits the business facts and the applicable KoB row. Price should be assessed after eligibility has been established.

faq.q: Does perpetual validity mean no future payments?
faq.a: No. The March 2026 framework retains annual fee obligations and applicable return requirements. Check the live FoSCoS account's payment position and instructions.

faq.q: Can a consultant guarantee an FSSAI licence?
faq.a: A consultant can help assess, prepare and respond to queries. The competent authority makes the regulatory decision; myfoodlicense.com does not guarantee approval.

faq.q: Which portal should I use to apply?
faq.a: Use the official FoSCoS portal. The consultancy website provides assistance and information.

posts.title: FSSAI Registration vs State Licence vs Central Licence: Which One Do You Need?
posts.description: Compare FSSAI registration, State and Central licences using the revised 2026 turnover bands and important Kind-of-Business exceptions.
posts.lede: Use the revised 2026 turnover bands only after checking your business activity. Many ordinary activities follow the registration–State–Central progression, while several KoBs have their own licensing route regardless of turnover.
posts.body:
The 2026 comparison table

The turnover order is effective from 1 April 2026. The following table summarises its general bands; apply them through the detailed KoB eligibility table. Official turnover order.

CategoryGeneral annual-turnover bandDecision to make first
RegistrationUp to ₹1.5 croreDoes this activity permit registration?
State licenceAbove ₹1.5 crore, up to ₹50 croreDoes a special KoB row override the band?
Central licenceAbove ₹50 croreIs Central licensing already mandatory for this activity?

Think of the turnover bands as a sorting step after activity identification. They should not be used to decide that every business below the first boundary qualifies for registration. The distinction matters most when the business imports food, operates through a specialised manufacturing route or combines several functions.

The activity exceptions that change the answer

The revised table lists Importer, E-Commerce, proprietary-food manufacturing, supplements/nutraceuticals and non-specified foods under Central licensing without a turnover threshold restriction. A multi-state Head Office/Registered Office has a separate Central row. Clubs/canteens and caterers have distinct rows too. Check the complete April 2026 KoB table.

The practical lesson is to describe your role precisely. Selling through an online marketplace and operating an e-commerce food business are questions that need factual assessment. Record who owns the stock, who takes orders, who handles the food and which entity provides the platform. Do not jump from “I use the internet” to an unsupported licensing conclusion.

Similarly, “catering,” “home kitchen” and “restaurant” should not be treated as interchangeable labels. How meals are prepared, supplied and served can help establish the correct row. If the business fits an exception, document the row that applies instead of trying to fit it into a generic turnover calculator.

Check the original table: some rows have qualifications that disappear in short summaries. Where the route is unclear, ask for a written activity assessment before filing or purchasing a service package.

How to choose the right category in practice

Use a short decision worksheet. The aim is to make the conclusion reproducible: another person should be able to read your business description, identify the same issues and understand why the selected row fits.

  1. Identify the applicant. Record the legal entity or individual, rather than only the consumer-facing brand.
  2. Describe each premises. Note the address, the operation at the site and the entity responsible for it.
  3. List actual activities. Distinguish making food, repacking it, importing it, storing it and selling it.
  4. Review product classification. For a manufacturer, identify whether the proposed range belongs to a specialised product route.
  5. Read the matching KoB row. Check its exceptions before applying a turnover boundary.
  6. Confirm in the current FoSCoS application. Investigate a discrepancy instead of selecting a convenient alternative.

Give the worksheet a review date. Revisit it if the operation changes. A company that initially sells finished products may later start repacking; a local brand may later import an ingredient or launch a supplement range. Reusing the first conclusion without reviewing those changes can create a gap between the paperwork and the real business.

Worked scenarios: the facts that matter

Hypothetical scenario: a neighbourhood retailer

A shop sells sealed food products obtained from suppliers and reports annual turnover of ₹40 lakh. Begin with the retailer row and its registration eligibility. If the shop also starts repacking bulk foods under its own brand, reassess the added activity before assuming the original route still covers the full operation.

Hypothetical scenario: an importer with small sales

A new business proposes importing packaged snacks and expects ₹25 lakh in annual sales. The activity assessment comes before the turnover sorting step. Check the importer-specific route, and plan product and consignment compliance separately from the business authorisation.

Hypothetical scenario: a packaged-food manufacturer

A manufacturer expects ₹80 lakh in sales and describes its range as “innovative snacks.” The important missing information is the formulation and applicable product classification. Establish that first, then use the correct manufacturing row. The marketing description cannot establish eligibility by itself.

These examples show a method, not a regulatory determination for a reader's business. A useful assessment states its assumptions. If a missing fact could change the answer, make that fact an action item rather than concealing the uncertainty.

How should existing businesses approach the 2026 transition?

The implementation FAQ describes migration based on self-declarations, preservation of the existing number, no migration fee for the revised thresholds and adjustment of prepaid fees. Check the actual FoSCoS account for the transition position of your certificate. See the official migration FAQ.

Before making a declaration, collect the relevant business information and review whether the activity itself has changed. A reduction in expected eligibility category does not answer a question about a new product, another premises or an inaccurate activity entry. Keep those issues distinct in the work plan.

Save the certificate and account status before and after any transition action. This provides a reference when communicating with suppliers, marketplaces or internal teams. If different systems display conflicting information, investigate which document and status each system is using.

Does a Central licence automatically cover the whole business?

A Central licence should not be treated as a general pass for every entity, location and product associated with a brand. Review the actual certificate and the arrangements at each site. Map the manufacturing partner, brand owner, importer and warehouse where relevant.

For a company operating in several places, prepare a table with one row per location. Add the legal operator, the activities, the authorisation currently held and the questions requiring review. This is more useful than an inventory of certificate numbers without context.

If the brand uses a contract manufacturer, obtain the manufacturer details and describe the contractual responsibilities. The brand's commercial relationship with the factory should be understandable from the evidence. The factory's certificate does not, by itself, resolve every regulatory question for the brand.

Choose assistance by scope, after eligibility

Compare consultancy proposals against the work you need. A proposal should identify the applicant and site, the activity assessment, the document preparation, the filing support and the handling of queries. Ask what additional work would be charged if the first business description turns out to be incomplete.

myfoodlicense.com provides State licence application support and multiple-KoB assessment. The assessment is useful when the business combines functions or when a short turnover-based answer would leave important facts unresolved.

Once the route is agreed, use the document preparation guide and the government-versus-professional fee guide to prepare the application. This keeps category selection, evidence and cost planning connected without allowing the cheapest quotation to decide the legal route.

faq.q: What is the FSSAI registration turnover limit in 2026?
faq.a: The general revised band is turnover up to ₹1.5 crore, effective from 1 April 2026. Check whether the activity-specific KoB row permits registration.

faq.q: Can a low-turnover importer use basic registration?
faq.a: Check the importer row, which has a Central licensing route irrespective of turnover. A small sales forecast does not settle importer eligibility.

faq.q: Is exactly ₹1.5 crore inside the registration band?
faq.a: The general registration band includes ₹1.5 crore. State licensing starts above that amount, subject to the applicable activity row.

faq.q: Is exactly ₹50 crore inside the State band?
faq.a: The general State band includes ₹50 crore. The Central turnover band begins above it, subject to activity-specific requirements.

faq.q: Can I decide from turnover alone?
faq.a: Start with the actual activities, product route and premises. Use turnover only after checking the matching official eligibility row.

posts.title: Documents Required for FSSAI Registration and Licence: A Practical Checklist
posts.description: Prepare registration and licence documents by business activity, check common mismatches and download a practical FSSAI application checklist.
posts.lede: For registration, the official short list covers a photograph, government-issued photo ID and business-address evidence where applicable. Licence applications use an activity-specific document list, so build your file from the selected KoB and the live FoSCoS upload requirements.
posts.body:
Documents for an FSSAI registration certificate

The official registration checklist identifies three items: a photo, government-issued photo identification such as Aadhaar, PAN or voter ID, and proof of the business-activity address if it differs from the address on the photo ID. Read the FoSCoS registration document list.

This is a registration document list, not a complete description of every business fact you will enter online. Prepare the business name, address, activity description and contact information separately. Check which declarations and other fields the current application presents.

ItemPreparation check
Applicant photographUse a clear image of the correct person and follow the live upload instructions.
Government photo IDCheck legibility and consistency with the applicant details entered.
Conditional business-address proofConfirm whether the business operates at an address different from the ID address.

Do not turn examples of acceptable identification into a demand for every listed identity document. The objective is to provide the evidence required for the actual application, with enough clarity to avoid avoidable questions.

Why a licence application needs a KoB-specific checklist

FSSAI's standardized-document order directs the use of the Kind-of-Business document list. A generic page listing every possible certificate is a poor substitute for the relevant row. Read the standardized-document order.

First establish the licence category and activities, then read the corresponding list. A retailer, a manufacturing unit and an importer do different work. Their evidence should answer different questions. Where the portal requests a document, read any conditional note beside it before deciding how to respond.

The official State-licence page lists activity-relevant evidence such as layout and equipment information, the product range, conditional water-analysis documentation and food-safety management material. Apply the conditions relevant to the selected KoB, and use the current upload list for the specific application. Read the official State-licence document list.

Use the matrix as a control document. Make one list of required uploads and another of the information useful for preparing the application. This prevents helpful background material from being mistaken for a universally compulsory upload.

A working checklist for State and Central licence preparation

The following is an original preparation worksheet. Its questions help organise the file; they do not replace the official conditional document requirements.

FolderQuestions to resolve
Applicant and authority to actWho is applying? Who may sign and operate the application account?
Business constitutionWhat is the legal form, and which records establish it?
PremisesWhere does the activity occur, and what evidence supports use of that site?
OperationsWhat activities are proposed, and what information does the selected KoB request?
ProductsWhich products are included, and has their regulatory classification been reviewed?
Special conditionsAre there activity-specific approvals, certificates or declarations to address?
Submission recordCan the team reproduce the final application and all files uploaded with it?

For each entry, assign a person responsible for obtaining the evidence. Record whether it is available, needs correction, is conditional or requires clarification. This creates a practical task list for an accountant, operations manager, landlord and consultant to work from together.

Download the application preparation checklist

Prepare manufacturing evidence from the actual operation

A useful premises layout should make the proposed operation understandable. Begin with the actual rooms and movement of materials, rather than copying a layout from a different factory. Label the areas in terms the operations team recognises so that the drawing and the physical site can be compared.

Prepare an equipment inventory using clear equipment names and the information requested for the application. Review it with the person who understands the process. If the planned production relies on equipment that has not yet been finalised, resolve the factual basis before making a declaration.

Collect product information in a consistent spreadsheet. Give each proposed product a descriptive name, its internal SKU if relevant, and the classification questions still outstanding. A marketing presentation full of brand names will not help much if the filing team needs to understand what is manufactured.

Where a requested water report or other test document is relevant, check what was sampled, where the sample came from, the report date and the report's scope. A report should answer the intended question. A document that happens to mention water is not necessarily evidence about the water used in the proposed process.

Use these preparation checks to assess relevance and consistency. The official requirement and any authority query should determine the evidence submitted; this guide does not prescribe a single testing package for every operation.

Check the legal entity, signatory and premises together

Create a one-page identity sheet containing the exact legal name, applicant type, authorised contact and premises address. Use it when comparing supporting papers. This makes differences easier to spot before they are repeated across an online application.

If the brand name differs from the legal entity name, explain the relationship in your working file. If the premises is rented, inspect whether the address and parties are understandable from the available evidence. Where a company representative is acting for the applicant, check the authority supporting that role.

Hypothetical example

A company opens a warehouse in “Unit B-12,” but a premises document only identifies the industrial estate. Its working file records the missing unit detail and the evidence needed to connect the occupied unit with the legal applicant. This is a document-review example, not an actual client or a guaranteed reason for rejection.

Be especially careful with documents assembled from different years. The business may have changed partners, directors or addresses since the first folder was created. Resolve the current facts before treating a previously accepted scan as suitable for a new filing.

Use a pre-upload quality check

Review the content before the file format. A perfectly compressed scan can still show the wrong premises. Once the evidence is correct, compare the upload version with the original and check that it remains legible.

  • Confirm that the document belongs to the right applicant and site.
  • Check that every page, signature and relevant attachment is included.
  • Use filenames that explain the contents without replacing the document's identity.
  • Follow the file type and size instructions currently shown in the portal.
  • Check dates and validity where the document has them.
  • Keep a copy of the precise version submitted.

Avoid universal claims such as “every upload must be below this size” unless you have checked the relevant field. Different screens or document types may have different instructions. Work from the live prompts and preserve a record if a technical problem needs to be reported.

What if the application is returned for documents?

Read the query as a request to establish something. It may concern identity, lawful premises use, a manufacturing process or a product's regulatory position. Identify the underlying issue before replacing files.

Prepare a reply with four columns: issue raised, factual response, supporting evidence and action completed. If a document is unavailable, establish why and determine the correct next step rather than uploading an unrelated paper. Keep the original query and the reply together.

FSSAI's licensing FAQ explains that physical copies need not routinely be submitted to regional or State offices after the online application. Use current directions and the specific authority communication for the application in question. See the official FAQ on document submission.

For assistance, myfoodlicense.com offers registration document support and application clarification and resubmission support. Define whether the engagement covers initial preparation, technical corrections, authority queries or all of those stages.

Keep a record after filing

Save the submitted application, the uploaded evidence, the reference number, payment acknowledgements and subsequent communications in one controlled folder. Limit editing of the submission record; use new versions for later corrections.

Keep a change log for the underlying business information. When a premises, signatory or product range changes, the log gives the filing team a starting point for assessing any regulatory action. That is more reliable than remembering which scan was used months earlier.

faq.q: Is a GST certificate compulsory for every FSSAI registration?
faq.a: Do not assume it is. Use the official registration list and the current application's instructions; requirements depend on the route and the relevant business facts.

faq.q: Do all licence applicants need a water-test report?
faq.a: Treat water-analysis evidence as an activity-dependent requirement. Check the official KoB list and the circumstances of the proposed operation.

faq.q: Can I submit the same documents for a retailer and a manufacturer?
faq.a: Some identity and entity evidence may overlap, but the activity-specific requirements differ. Build each checklist from the matching official KoB list.

faq.q: Where can I find the current upload limits?
faq.a: Read the instructions next to the relevant upload field in FoSCoS. Avoid applying a file-size figure taken from an unrelated or old screen.

faq.q: Can I use a rented premises?
faq.a: Prepare evidence supporting the applicant's use of the actual site and check the required premises documents for the application. A residential or rented location also needs assessment of any other applicable local requirements.

posts.title: FSSAI Licence Fees in 2026: Government Fee vs Professional Fee Explained
posts.description: Understand current FSSAI annual government fees, perpetual validity, professional charges and the questions to ask before paying for an application.
posts.lede: Separate the official government charge from the fee for consultancy work. FSSAI's 2026 framework provides perpetual validity, but the government fee remains an ongoing obligation; a service quotation should explain both parts of the cost.
posts.body:
Current government fees: the starting figures

The April 2026 official update reports the implemented fee structure. Read it alongside the applicable eligibility row and the live portal payment demand. The figures below are annual government charges, not quotations from myfoodlicense.com. Official April 2026 update.

RouteAnnual government chargeBudgeting note
Registration, ordinarily₹100Check fee-waiver or special registration rows.
State licence, ordinarily₹5,000Select the correct activity before estimating.
Central licence, ordinarily₹7,500Separate business licensing from product or import-clearance work.
Railways/Central Government agency Central licensing entries₹2,000Use the exact qualifying row; this is not the ordinary Central fee.

The revised KoB table also shows waived registration fees for specified activities, including hawkers and Anganwadi centres. Eligibility for a waiver must be established from the applicable row rather than assumed from the business's size. Check the full fee and eligibility table.

When comparing this guide with an older webpage, check the source date and the selected activity. Historic State fee tiers or a total for a multi-year renewal may describe an earlier system. Save the current official row and the portal receipt with the cost approval so the basis is clear.

What perpetual validity means for cost planning

The March 2026 amendment removes periodic expiry from the revised framework while retaining annual fees and applicable returns. Specified failures can lead to deemed suspension. Do not interpret perpetual validity as a one-time payment buying unrestricted operation forever. Read amended regulation 2.1.7.

The implementation FAQ says fees can be selected for any number of years at once and paid at any time of year. It also describes adjustment of prepaid fees when the revised thresholds change eligibility. Read the official fee FAQ.

Build a budget that identifies the covered payment period and the next action shown in the account. Avoid inventing a universal payment deadline from a consultant's webpage. Reconcile the certificate, payment history and live FoSCoS status for the actual business.

Hypothetical arithmetic illustration

If the applicable annual government charge is ₹5,000 and the account permits payment for three years, the simple government-fee component is ₹15,000. This calculation excludes professional work and any other applicable charges. It illustrates multiplication, not a personalised payment demand.

What does the professional fee pay for?

A professional fee should buy identifiable work. Ask whether it includes selecting the application route, checking the papers, preparing entries, uploading documents, tracking progress and responding to questions. These stages require different amounts of effort depending on the business facts.

A simple application with consistent papers may need less preparation than a manufacturing file with unresolved classification and premises issues. A price comparison is useful only when the scope is comparable. A low initial quote can be incomplete if essential work is charged separately.

Ask the provider to describe the deliverables in writing. For example, “document review” should explain whether the provider merely checks that scans exist or examines their consistency with the applicant and activity. “Query handling” should explain the extent of support and what happens if a query reveals a different business model.

myfoodlicense.com provides State licence application assistance and Central licence application assistance. Request a scope matched to the business before treating the total as a finished budget.

Additional work that may need its own budget

Some projects involve work beyond business licensing. A new packaged-food brand may need product classification, formulation assessment, label review, testing or clarification of ingredient status. An importer also needs to plan the particular product and shipment. List those questions before assuming an application service includes them.

Possible cost itemQuestion to ask
Product classificationIs the proposed food's regulatory route already established?
Formulation or ingredient reviewDoes the quote include evaluating the actual recipe and specifications?
Laboratory workWhich tests, samples and laboratory charges are within scope?
Artwork reviewHow many SKUs, pack sizes and revision rounds are covered?
Authority clarificationWhich communications and response stages are included?
Premises preparationDoes the business need operational work outside the application service?

This is a planning list, not a statement that every applicant must pay for every item. Mark each item as necessary, optional, already complete or awaiting assessment. That produces a more realistic budget than adding a generic “compliance package” to every application.

How to compare two licence-service quotations

Create a simple comparison sheet with the applicant, premises and activities at the top. Ask each provider to quote against those same facts. If one provider assumes a different KoB or excludes a site, investigate the difference before comparing prices.

  1. Separate government and professional amounts. Ask how the government payment will be acknowledged.
  2. Identify taxes and conditional costs. Ask what the total includes and what can change it.
  3. Define document preparation. Establish who obtains missing evidence and who corrects discrepancies.
  4. Define query support. Clarify the support included if the authority requests further information.
  5. Confirm access and handover. Decide how the business receives the application reference, receipts and final record.
  6. Review the service terms. Understand cancellation, refunds and additional-work charges before instructing the provider.

A proposal should not imply that a higher fee can buy official approval. Evaluate the explanation of the route and the quality of preparation. A good scope makes both the provider's work and the client's responsibilities visible.

Prepare the inputs that make a quote meaningful

Supply the business activity, legal structure, location, expected or relevant turnover information and proposed product range. Mention imports, online operations, contract manufacturing and additional premises if they are part of the plan.

Tell the provider whether documents are ready and whether there is an existing application or authority query. Share the actual query rather than a summary such as “documents rejected.” An accurate initial brief reduces the chance of pricing for the wrong task.

Keep a list of unresolved questions. If the product classification is unclear, ask whether the first engagement is an assessment or a complete filing. Separating those stages can make the work more reviewable and prevent a service fee from being mistaken for a guarantee.

Keep payment evidence and monitor the account

Maintain a cost record with the government acknowledgement, the professional invoice and any agreed additional work. Match each payment to the applicant and application reference. Do not rely only on a message saying “payment done.”

For an existing business, review the current account before paying for a service described as renewal. Establish whether the task concerns annual fees, transition, modification or another issue. The name used in a quotation should accurately describe the work being done under the current framework.

Use the category comparison to resolve eligibility and the document checklist to identify preparation work. Together they provide a stronger basis for a quotation than a turnover figure and an urgent request for the cheapest licence.

posts.title: How to Apply for an FSSAI Licence on FoSCoS: Step by Step
posts.description: Apply for an FSSAI registration or licence through the official FoSCoS portal after identifying your premises, Kind of Business and current eligibility
posts.lede: Apply for an FSSAI registration or licence through the official FoSCoS portal after identifying your premises, Kind of Business and current eligibility. A complete application must describe the actual business and contain consistent evidence; paying the fee is only one step.
posts.body:
Start with the premises and activity

Write down the legal applicant, operating address, activities and products before opening the form. A manufacturer selling its own products, a trader importing finished packs and a restaurant preparing meals have different application requirements. Use the revised eligibility table rather than a turnover calculator that ignores special KoB rows. Read the current eligibility table.

Prepare the application evidence

Create folders for identity, constitution, premises and activity-specific evidence. Match names and addresses across attachments. For manufacturing, prepare the product list and any requested layout, equipment, water or technical-person information. Registration and licensing document lists differ; upload what the selected route actually asks for. Use the documents guide.

Complete the official form

Open FoSCoS, select the relevant application route and state, and enter the business details. Review the KoB selection, applicant contacts and products before continuing. Form A relates to registration and Form B to licensing under the regulatory framework. Portal screens may change, so use the labels currently displayed rather than following an old screenshot word for word.

Pay, track and answer queries

Pay through the official workflow and retain the payment record and application reference. A bank debit alone is insufficient evidence that the application was submitted. Track the actual application status and open any authority query. Prepare a response against each requested correction, replace affected documents consistently and retain the submitted version.

Check the issued certificate

Confirm the number, entity, premises, KoBs and endorsed products against the application. Set up annual-fee and applicable-return reminders. The 2026 perpetual-validity model still requires compliance; do not interpret the absence of an ordinary expiry date as permission to ignore fees or changes. Read the 2026 licensing amendment.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A small sauce manufacturer prepares identity documents but selects Retailer because it also sells direct. Before filing, the owner maps the processing activity and chooses the applicable manufacturing route. The product list, premises evidence and fee are then reviewed together. This prevents a clean-looking application from describing the wrong business.

Your practical checklist

  • Confirm the applicant and operating address.
  • Map every actual KoB before selecting the route.
  • Check special eligibility rows and product requirements.
  • Upload readable, matching attachments.
  • Save the payment receipt and submission reference.
  • Review queries and the issued certificate.

Download this preparation checklist

faq.a: Use the official FoSCoS portal linked in this guide. Check the domain before entering identity or payment information.

faq.a: Yes. A consultant can assist with assessment and preparation, but the official application and authority decision remain separate.

faq.a: No. Verify submission status and wait for the actual certificate or authority decision.

faq.q: What if my application is reverted?
faq.a: Read each query, correct the underlying issue and submit a documented response within the deadline shown.

faq.q: Can I use old turnover limits?
faq.a: No. Assess the current 2026 KoB row, including special activity and product rules.

posts.title: FSSAI Licence Renewal in 2026: Perpetual Validity, Annual Fees and Legacy Certificates
posts.description: FSSAI renewal guidance changed in 2026: licences and registrations issued under the new framework have perpetual validity, subject to continuing obligations
posts.lede: FSSAI renewal guidance changed in 2026: licences and registrations issued under the new framework have perpetual validity, subject to continuing obligations. Existing certificates need a transition check. Annual fees, applicable returns and suspension status now matter more than copying an old renewal countdown.
posts.body:
What changed in 2026?

The March 2026 amendment replaces the ordinary fixed-validity model with perpetual validity unless an authorisation is suspended, cancelled or surrendered. FSSAI’s March FAQs explain the treatment of certificates issued on or after 1 April 2026. Read the notification and transition guidance together. Licensing amendment; transition FAQs.

What should an existing licence holder do?

Open the actual FoSCoS record and compare it with the certificate in your files. Record the old validity dates, issue date, fee history, current status and any migration instruction. A legacy PDF showing an expiry date does not explain every transition question. Do not assume that applying a new turnover threshold automatically completes all changes to your account.

Perpetual validity still requires payments and returns

Under the amended framework, failure to pay the annual fee or submit an applicable return leads to deemed suspension. The rules provide for revocation after the outstanding obligations and due penalties are resolved. Food business cannot continue during suspension. Keep fee and return evidence together, and identify whether D1 applies to your activities. Read the annual-return guide.

Avoid outdated late-fee advice

Old renewal articles commonly discuss fixed-year validity, renewal windows and late-renewal charges. Those passages cannot be applied mechanically to a new perpetual certificate. Distinguish a legacy renewal issue from an annual-fee default or a late return. Ask for a calculation tied to the actual authorisation and operative provision, rather than a single penalty number for every situation.

Build a continuing-compliance calendar

Assign an owner for fee checks, return applicability, contact details and modifications. Save receipts and acknowledgement records. Review operational changes such as a new site, ownership change or added product before treating them as covered. Perpetual validity keeps the authorisation alive under conditions; it does not enlarge its endorsed business scope.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A bakery owner finds a 2025 certificate with an expiry date and reads a blog saying renewal has disappeared. The owner checks the current account, obtains the applicable transition position and records fee obligations before making a filing decision. The decision is based on that certificate’s status, rather than either the old PDF or the headline alone.

Your practical checklist

  • Compare your certificate with the current FoSCoS account.
  • Record issue date, old validity and current status.
  • Check transition or migration instructions.
  • Confirm annual-fee payment history.
  • Assess return applicability and outstanding dues.
  • Do not operate under a suspended authorisation.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our Licence Renewal service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

headings.text: What should an existing licence holder do?
Perpetual validity still requires payments and returns

faq.q: Do new FSSAI licences need ordinary renewal?
faq.a: The 2026 framework provides perpetual validity, subject to fees, returns and other compliance conditions.

faq.q: Is my old licence automatically perpetual?
faq.a: Check the specific legacy record and current transition instructions before concluding that its old expiry date is irrelevant.

faq.q: Does perpetual validity mean no annual fee?
faq.a: No. Continuing fee obligations remain under the revised model.

faq.q: Can non-filing of a return suspend a licence?
faq.a: Yes, where that return applies; the amended validity provision links applicable-return defaults to deemed suspension.

faq.q: What should I do after suspension?
faq.a: Identify and resolve the exact grounds, retain the acknowledgement and verify restoration before resuming food business.

posts.title: FSSAI Registration for Home Bakers and Home Kitchens
posts.description: A home baker or home kitchen selling food needs the appropriate FSSAI authorisation for the actual activity
posts.lede: A home baker or home kitchen selling food needs the appropriate FSSAI authorisation for the actual activity. Operating from a residence, taking orders on WhatsApp or selling only at weekends does not by itself create an exemption. Start with the product, premises and current KoB criteria.
posts.body:
Describe what the home business actually does

Separate preparing fresh meals, baking packaged products, catering events and reselling another manufacturer’s packs. These activities can lead to different KoB selections and duties. Write down where ingredients are stored, where production occurs and how products reach customers. A residential address should accurately identify the food premises.

Check the current route

The general 2026 registration band extends to annual turnover up to ₹1.5 crore, but activity-specific rows can override the general bands. Catering and specialised manufactured foods are examples requiring a separate check. Do not select a registration route solely because the business has few orders. Use the revised KoB table.

Prepare documents that match the home premises

Gather the applicant’s identity, contact details and the evidence requested for the selected registration or licensing route. Establish the right to use the premises. Where another person owns the property, address that fact through appropriate supporting documents rather than changing the operating address to an unrelated shop.

Control hygiene in a shared kitchen

Separate business stock from household supplies, protect prepared food from pets and pests, manage cleaning and allergens, and choose storage suitable for the product. A domestic refrigerator is not evidence that every product remains safe through delivery. Plan holding time, transport and handling instructions together. Schedule 4 contains the applicable hygiene framework. Read the hygiene guide.

Review what customers receive

A prepacked cake mix, cookie pouch or jar sold as a retail product needs a category-specific label review. Freshly prepared order fulfilment needs its own presentation and information assessment. Do not reuse another bakery’s nutrition panel, shelf life or licence number. Keep the product identity, responsible business and customer claims accurate. Review the labelling guide.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A home baker sells custom cakes and also launches sealed cookie pouches for local shops. The owner reviews both activities, the packaging and the retail distribution arrangement. The cookie shelf life and allergen statement are assessed separately from the made-to-order cake menu. One business address does not make all product information interchangeable.

Your practical checklist

  • List meals, baking, catering and resale activities separately.
  • Use the current eligibility row.
  • Prepare evidence for the actual residence used.
  • Create cleaning, storage and allergen controls.
  • Assess labels for prepacked retail products.
  • Keep order, supplier and complaint records.

Download this preparation checklist

headings.text: Describe what the home business actually does
Prepare documents that match the home premises
Control hygiene in a shared kitchen

faq.q: Do home bakers need FSSAI registration?
faq.a: They need the appropriate authorisation for their food business; determine whether registration or a licence applies.

faq.q: Does selling through Instagram change this?
faq.a: The sales channel does not remove the underlying food-business obligations.

faq.q: Can I use my home address?
faq.a: Use the actual food premises and provide the evidence required for that premises and route.

faq.q: Do all homemade products need the same label?
faq.a: No. Product category, packaging and mode of sale affect the applicable declarations.

faq.q: Is occasional selling exempt?
faq.a: A small or intermittent business should assess the applicable route rather than assume an exemption.

posts.title: FSSAI Licence for Cloud Kitchens (Swiggy & Zomato Requirements)
posts.description: A cloud kitchen needs FSSAI authorisation for the premises where food is prepared
posts.lede: A cloud kitchen needs FSSAI authorisation for the premises where food is prepared. Delivery-only operation does not remove that requirement. Resolve the kitchen’s regulatory route first, then supply the certificate and business documents requested by Swiggy, Zomato or another platform.
posts.body:
One kitchen can trade through several brands

List the legal operator, preparation address, menus and virtual brand names. Platform storefronts do not establish separate licensed premises. Conversely, opening a second kitchen creates a premises question even when the same brand and menu are used. Keep site addresses consistent across the certificate, partner account and invoice records.

Use the correct food-service row

Choose the actual KoB and assess the revised 2026 criteria. A restaurant-style delivery kitchen and an event caterer should not automatically receive the same registration recommendation. The number of online listings is not a licence category. Check the current eligibility table.

Prepare onboarding documents

Swiggy’s partner page asks applicants to keep an FSSAI licence copy, menu, bank details, GSTIN and PAN ready. That is a platform list; tax applicability and the correct FSSAI route still need their own assessment. Platform requests can change, so confirm the current request in the official partner flow. Swiggy partner onboarding.

Manage the delivery journey

Map ingredient receipt, cooking, holding, packing and handover. Choose packaging and handling controls appropriate to hot meals, chilled desserts or other products. Record complaints and investigate temperature, leakage or contamination issues. A food-safety plan should include dispatch practices, rather than stop at the moment cooking ends.

Keep listings and certificates aligned

Use accurate food descriptions and claims, avoid misleading images or ingredient omissions, and update the platform when regulatory details change. If the certificate has perpetual validity but an onboarding form demands an expiry date, raise a documented support query. Do not invent a date to pass validation. Understand the 2026 validity change.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A cloud kitchen operates two virtual brands from one site and then rents a second production unit. The owner maps the existing authorisation to the first site and assesses a separate route for the new unit. Each partner listing is linked to the correct preparation location, so customers and platforms receive consistent business information.

Your practical checklist

  • Map legal operator, brands and each preparation site.
  • Assess the correct food-service KoB.
  • Gather the current official partner document list.
  • Review holding, packing and delivery controls.
  • Match platform details to the certificate.
  • Escalate certificate-date validation issues with evidence.

Download this preparation checklist

headings.text: One kitchen can trade through several brands

faq.q: Does a delivery-only kitchen need FSSAI authorisation?
faq.a: Yes. The preparation premises and actual business activity determine the route.

faq.q: Does every virtual brand need a separate licence?
faq.a: Assess the operator, premises and endorsed activities; a storefront name alone does not settle the licensing question.

faq.q: Can one certificate cover two kitchen addresses?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Each operating premises needs an appropriate assessment.

faq.q: Does Swiggy approval equal FSSAI approval?
faq.a: No. Platform onboarding and regulatory authorisation are separate decisions.

faq.q: What if the platform wants an expiry date?
faq.a: Provide the current certificate and ask official partner support how its form handles perpetual-validity records.

posts.title: FSSAI Licence for Restaurants, Cafés and Caterers
posts.description: Restaurants, cafés and caterers need an FSSAI route matched to their actual business
posts.lede: Restaurants, cafés and caterers need an FSSAI route matched to their actual business. Under the revised 2026 table, catering has a different eligibility row from ordinary restaurant operations. Assess event catering, café service and each premises before choosing registration or a licence.
posts.body:
Separate service models before comparing turnover

A café serving meals from its own premises, a restaurant delivering orders and a caterer serving organised events can have different activity descriptions. Hotels also have separate criteria. Describe what happens at the kitchen, outlet and event site, and identify the responsible operator for each.

The catering exception matters

The current table places caterers up to ₹50 crore annual turnover in the State-licence row and above that figure in Central licensing; it does not provide the ordinary registration band for catering. Ordinary restaurant rows use the general bands, subject to location or other special conditions. Read the food-service rows.

Prepare a site-specific application

Document the entity, applicant authority, premises and applicable food-service requirements. A shared kitchen or hired event facility should have a clear responsibility arrangement. Do not assume a venue’s certificate automatically authorises an unrelated caterer’s operations. Explain your model before filing a simple restaurant application.

Prepare staff and records for inspection

Use the relevant Schedule 4 requirements for catering and food service. Food receipt, preparation, water, cleaning, personal hygiene and waste handling should work during peak service. Maintain records staff can explain. For State or Central licensed premises, review trained-supervisor requirements. Read the FoSTaC guide.

Review food information and changes

Assess menu claims and any applicable display requirements by establishment type. Selling packaged sauces or retail snacks alongside café meals creates additional product and label questions. A new kitchen, change of operator or added activity should trigger a licensing review before business details drift away from the authorisation.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A small café starts taking wedding catering contracts. Its owner initially assumes the existing low-turnover registration covers every order. The catering row prompts a review of the added activity and State-licence requirement, while the operating team prepares event transport, holding and service procedures.

Your practical checklist

  • Describe café, restaurant, hotel and catering activities accurately.
  • Check the catering exception in the current table.
  • Assess every kitchen and event responsibility arrangement.
  • Prepare Schedule 4 operating controls.
  • Check supervisor and display requirements.
  • Review packaged-product sales separately.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our State FSSAI Licence – New service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

headings.text: Separate service models before comparing turnover
Prepare staff and records for inspection

faq.q: Can a small caterer use ordinary registration bands?
faq.a: The 2026 catering row requires a separate assessment; it does not list the ordinary registration band.

faq.q: Is a café automatically a restaurant for licensing?
faq.a: Assess its actual food-service activity and any other operations.

faq.q: Does a hotel licence depend only on turnover?
faq.a: No. The current table contains hotel-specific criteria.

faq.q: Can I sell packaged products from a café?
faq.a: Assess the relevant activities, product compliance and retail labels before adding them.

faq.q: Do restaurant employees need hygiene training?
faq.a: Training and supervision form part of compliance; State and Central licensed businesses should assess FoSTaC supervisor requirements.

posts.keyword: fssai license for online food business
posts.title: FSSAI Licence for E-commerce and Online Food Sellers (Amazon, Flipkart, Quick Commerce)
posts.description: An online food seller must assess its own food-business activities, while an e-commerce food platform has a separate Central-licensing row
posts.lede: An online food seller must assess its own food-business activities, while an e-commerce food platform has a separate Central-licensing row. Selling through Amazon or another marketplace does not automatically make every seller the platform operator. Manufacturing, relabelling, storage and import activities still matter.
posts.body:
Distinguish seller from platform

Draw the transaction: who owns the website or marketplace, who sells the food, who manufactures it and where stock is stored. An online presence is a sales channel, but operating an e-commerce food business can create a specific KoB requirement. Resolve that boundary using the actual model rather than a blanket online-equals-Central rule.

Check every actual activity

The 2026 table lists E-Commerce for Central licensing without a turnover restriction. Other roles, such as ordinary retail, specialised manufacturing or importing, have their own rows. A D2C brand commissioning production may need a relabeller assessment even though it has no factory. Check activity-specific eligibility.

Prepare marketplace evidence

Amazon’s official grocery page requires FSSAI licence details and a declaration of compliance with food-safety standards. Its organic-product requirements create a separate certification question. Keep the food authorisation, product evidence and platform documents consistent. A platform’s approval does not establish that every claim or ingredient is compliant. Amazon grocery requirements.

Treat the listing as food information

Review title, pack images, ingredients, allergens, nutrition claims and business information across the listing and physical pack. Use the online declaration requirements that apply to your sale. Do not hide a required warning on an image that customers cannot read or use an outdated artwork version to advertise current stock.

Plan warehouse and stock changes

Identify who operates fulfilment facilities and who controls storage and shelf-life checks. New warehouses, outsourced storage and quick-commerce channels need an operational responsibility review. Assign someone to update regulatory certificates and product content when the recipe, pack or manufacturing site changes. Use the D2C compliance checklist.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A snack brand buys contract-manufactured packs and sells through its own site and a marketplace. It maps the manufacturer, brand-owner activities, website operation and fulfilment sites separately. That assessment identifies the licensing questions and the data each listing must reflect, rather than assuming the marketplace’s licence covers the brand.

Your practical checklist

  • Map seller, website operator, manufacturer and warehouses.
  • Resolve e-commerce and other KoBs separately.
  • Prepare current marketplace documents.
  • Match product listings to approved physical labels.
  • Define storage and shelf-life responsibilities.
  • Create a process for updating every channel.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our Marketplace Compliance Review service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

headings.text: Treat the listing as food information

faq.a: No. Assess your own activities and premises independently.

faq.a: Do not generalise. E-commerce operators have a special row; individual sellers require an assessment of their own model.

faq.q: Does a website need label information?
faq.a: Assess applicable online declaration requirements and ensure customers receive accurate food information.

faq.q: Can a home business sell online?
faq.a: Assess licensing, product compliance and current platform eligibility before listing.

faq.q: Does organic certification matter online?
faq.a: Yes. Organic claims and relevant platform documentation require a separate certification assessment.

posts.title: FSSAI Licence for Food Importers: Central Licence, IEC and Process
posts.description: A food importer requires the Central-licence route in the 2026 KoB table, irrespective of turnover
posts.lede: A food importer requires the Central-licence route in the 2026 KoB table, irrespective of turnover. Licensing, IEC and shipment clearance are separate requirements. Obtain the correct business authorisation and establish Indian product compliance before placing a commercial import order.
posts.body:
Identify the legal importer

Confirm the entity that will import the food and appear in the Customs and commercial documents. Keep its name and address consistent with the application evidence. A foreign manufacturer’s certificate or an Indian distributor’s unrelated licence does not replace the importer’s own requirements.

Apply under the importer row

The revised table specifies Central licensing for Importer without a turnover threshold. Do not use the general registration band to assess a small first shipment. Prepare the documents requested for the importer route, including the applicable IEC evidence. Importer eligibility; Import Regulations.

IEC and FSSAI have different jobs

IEC is part of the foreign-trade framework administered through DGFT. FSSAI licensing authorises the relevant food-business activity. Customs filing and FSSAI clearance assess the consignment. Make a document matrix showing which evidence serves which purpose, and ensure identifiers refer to the same importing entity.

Check the product before shipment

Review the complete recipe, ingredient specifications, additives, category, claims and Indian label. A product legally sold abroad may need reformulation, approval or different presentation in India. Check remaining shelf life and shipment conditions before accepting dispatch. Read the ingredient-permission comparison.

Continue compliance after the first import

Maintain shipment, batch, supplier and distribution records. Assess annual D1 applicability for the importer and other obligations under the current validity framework. Adding local repacking, storage or distribution operations can create further KoB and premises questions. The importer licence is not a universal permit for every activity. Follow the clearance workflow.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A company imports a limited batch of premium snacks and expects its low turnover to qualify for registration. The importer row instead leads it to Central licensing. Before shipment, it checks the overseas additive specifications and prepares an India-specific label review, so business licensing and product clearance are addressed separately.

Your practical checklist

  • Confirm the legal importer and document identifiers.
  • Select the Central importer route.
  • Prepare IEC and current application evidence.
  • Review the complete product for India.
  • Plan labels, shelf life and shipment records.
  • Assess D1 and added local activities.

Download this preparation checklist

headings.text: IEC and FSSAI have different jobs
Continue compliance after the first import

faq.a: Yes. The current Importer row has no turnover restriction.

faq.q: Is IEC the same as an FSSAI licence?
faq.a: No. They serve different foreign-trade and food-business purposes.

faq.q: Does the licence clear every shipment?
faq.a: No. Consignment clearance remains a separate process.

faq.q: Can I import a product permitted in Europe?
faq.a: First establish its compliance with Indian product, ingredient, additive and label requirements.

faq.q: Do importers file D1?
faq.a: Licensed importing activities are within the annual-return framework; assess the relevant year and account obligations.

posts.title: FSSAI Licence for Food Manufacturers: 2026 Eligibility, Categories and Documents
posts.description: For food manufacturing in 2026, start with the current manufacturing KoB row and product route
posts.lede: For food manufacturing in 2026, start with the current manufacturing KoB row and product route. Old production-capacity thresholds copied from earlier guides can give the wrong result. The revised table uses turnover for many activities and retains special rules for particular products and operations.
posts.body:
Map the factory’s operations

Record the premises, processes, equipment, products and actual manufacturing arrangement. Processing, repacking and relabelling are different activities even when finished packs look similar. Establish whether the applicant owns production, commissions another factory or handles bulk product locally.

Read the revised eligibility row

The April 2026 table must govern the route assessment. Many ordinary manufacturing rows now use revised turnover bands. Proprietary foods, health supplements and nutraceuticals, non-specified foods, Ayurveda Aahara and other listed specialised activities have Central requirements without a turnover restriction. Milling and export operations also need their own row review. Current manufacturing criteria.

Classification comes before the product list

Check whether each product meets a food standard, belongs to a specialised category or needs approval. A food-category code helps identify applicable provisions but does not establish that the recipe is legal. Keep the classification decision and ingredient evidence with the list submitted for endorsement. Use the classification guide.

Prepare site and technical evidence

Follow the live KoB document requirements for constitution, layout, equipment, premises and applicable technical or water evidence. Define the process flow and hygiene controls before treating the application as a document-upload exercise. Required evidence should describe the same facility that officers would inspect.

Plan post-licence duties

Build systems for batch traceability, testing, appropriate production records and annual returns. The June 2026 amendment changes particular licence conditions, including manufacturing-related records. Check the actual scope of each condition rather than imposing every factory requirement on every trader. June 2026 amendment.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A manufacturer uses a dated calculator based on tonnes per day, then adds a proprietary snack to its product list. Reviewing the 2026 table and product route changes the licensing assessment. The owner updates the proposed application, while keeping capacity data for the facility evidence where it remains relevant.

Your practical checklist

  • Map manufacture, processing, repacking and relabelling.
  • Use the revised KoB criteria.
  • Identify specialised products and exceptions.
  • Prepare classification and formulation records.
  • Match layout and technical evidence to the site.
  • Set up testing, traceability and return records.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our State FSSAI Licence – New service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

headings.text: Classification comes before the product list

faq.q: Is production capacity irrelevant now?
faq.a: It can remain relevant to site and technical assessment. Do not use obsolete capacity thresholds to select the licence route.

faq.q: Do proprietary manufacturers need Central licensing?
faq.a: The current table lists proprietary-food manufacturing under Central licensing irrespective of turnover.

faq.q: Can one factory make several categories?
faq.a: Assess the endorsed products, applicable conditions and each manufacturing activity.

faq.q: Does an endorsed product list prove recipe compliance?
faq.a: No. Ingredient, additive, standard and claim compliance require their own review.

faq.q: What records should I prepare?
faq.a: Use the applicable licence conditions and product risks to plan production, supplier, testing and distribution records.

posts.title: FSSAI Licence for Exporters: Do You Need One?
posts.description: Food exporters must assess the export-related KoB that matches their role
posts.lede: Food exporters must assess the export-related KoB that matches their role. The 2026 table specifies Central licensing for listed export activities without a turnover restriction. A merchant exporter, export manufacturer and certified 100% export-oriented unit are distinct business models.
posts.body:
Identify the exporter’s role

A merchant exporter buys goods made by another manufacturer. An export manufacturer produces food for overseas sale. A 100% EOU has a particular recognised status and conditions. Write down the actual supply chain and avoid selecting EOU merely because you intend to export all current stock.

Read the export eligibility rows

The current table lists Merchant/Trader Exporter, Exporter-Manufacturer and 100% EOU with Central licensing. The EOU description includes its recognised certificate and export-only product context. Product standards and domestic sale questions need a separate assessment. Read the export rows.

Separate Indian authorisation from destination compliance

An Indian FSSAI licence does not approve a product for every overseas market. Destination rules may cover ingredients, labels, health certificates, establishments or customer requirements. Prepare a market-specific checklist based on the food and country, rather than treating a foreign buyer’s artwork approval as the complete compliance decision.

Keep supplier and batch evidence

Merchant exporters need a clear link between the supplier, manufacturing premises, product specifications and exported batches. Manufacturers need production and testing records suited to their products. Maintain invoices, shipment records and any certificates actually required by the trade or destination. Avoid adding generic export certificates to the file without checking their applicability.

Review returns and domestic activity

Licensed export-manufacturers are within the annual-return framework. If export-only goods or a certified EOU arrangement changes to include domestic sales, review the applicable product and licence conditions before release. Different market labels must be controlled so export stock does not accidentally enter domestic channels with unsuitable declarations.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A trader buying packaged tea for an overseas customer initially describes itself as a manufacturer. Its supply-chain review identifies the merchant-exporter role and the actual licensed tea producer. The file then links supplier batches to shipment documents, while destination label requirements are reviewed separately.

Your practical checklist

  • Distinguish merchant exporter, manufacturer and certified EOU.
  • Check the current Central eligibility row.
  • Identify supplier and batch records.
  • Review destination-market requirements.
  • Assess D1 applicability.
  • Control export-only and domestic stock separately.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our Central FSSAI Licence – New service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

headings.text: Separate Indian authorisation from destination compliance

faq.q: Do merchant exporters need an FSSAI route?
faq.a: Yes. The current export-trader row specifies Central licensing.

faq.q: Is every exporter a 100% EOU?
faq.a: No. EOU status has its own recognised conditions and documentary requirements.

faq.q: Does FSSAI approval establish overseas compliance?
faq.a: No. Destination-country and shipment requirements need a separate review.

faq.q: Do exporter-manufacturers file annual returns?
faq.a: They are within the relevant D1 framework; confirm the reporting year and applicable obligations.

faq.q: Can export-only stock be sold domestically?
faq.a: First assess Indian product requirements and any restrictions attached to the export-only arrangement.

posts.title: Kind of Business (KOB) on FoSCoS Explained and How to Pick the Right One
posts.description: Kind of Business, or KoB, describes what your food business does
posts.lede: Kind of Business, or KoB, describes what your food business does. It affects eligibility, documents and licence scope on FoSCoS. Choose it from actual operations: a food-category number identifies a product category and cannot replace an activity assessment.
posts.body:
Start with verbs rather than brand descriptions

Write whether the business manufactures, repacks, commissions production, imports, stores, transports, distributes, retails or serves food. Terms such as startup, D2C and organic brand describe positioning or channels; they do not explain every activity requiring assessment.

Map responsibility at each premises

Identify who controls processing, stock, invoices and customer delivery. A brand owner outsourcing production can have a different role from the factory. A warehouse operated by a separate entity cannot simply be treated as an invisible extension of the sales office. Document the actual contractual and operational arrangement.

Use the current definitions and criteria

FoSCoS and the revised KoB table provide activity descriptions and route criteria. Check every relevant row, including specialised manufacturing, import, e-commerce and head-office requirements. A low general turnover band does not override a Central-only KoB. Review the definitions and eligibility.

Keep KoB and product classification separate

KoB explains the business role. Product classification establishes the applicable food rules. Food-category codes help locate standards and additive permissions. Keep three distinct columns in your assessment so a correct product-category selection is not mistaken for permission to import, manufacture or relabel. Read the food-category guide.

Review the selection when the business changes

A new production contract, warehouse, import line or retail activity should trigger a scope review. Multiple activities at one premises may need to be included appropriately; multiple premises raise separate questions. Compare what the business actually does with what the certificate endorses, and resolve gaps before filing a modification.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A beverage brand calls itself an online retailer, but it commissions manufacture, imports one ingredient and operates a storage unit. Mapping the verbs reveals questions that the brand description concealed. The owner can then distinguish the manufacturing partner’s role, its own activities and the storage premises.

Your practical checklist

  • List the actual operating verbs.
  • Assign each activity to an entity and premises.
  • Check the current KoB definitions.
  • Review special eligibility rows.
  • Separate KoB from product category.
  • Compare operations with the certificate scope.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our Multiple KOB Assessment service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

headings.text: Start with verbs rather than brand descriptions
Use the current definitions and criteria
Keep KoB and product classification separate
Review the selection when the business changes

faq.q: What does KoB mean?
faq.a: Kind of Business: the activity or role of the food business in the supply chain.

faq.q: Is a category code the same as KoB?
faq.a: No. One describes the food category, the other the business activity.

faq.q: Can I choose the cheapest KoB?
faq.a: The selection must match actual operations and current eligibility.

faq.q: Can a brand owner be a relabeller?
faq.a: Its manufacturing arrangement may lead to that assessment; examine the actual role rather than the brand name.

faq.q: Can KoB change later?
faq.a: Yes. Added or changed activities require a review of the relevant modification or new-application route.
