posts.title: Running Several Kinds of Business Under One Licence
posts.description: Several food-business activities at the same premises can require multiple KoB endorsements in the appropriate authorisation
posts.lede: Several food-business activities at the same premises can require multiple KoB endorsements in the appropriate authorisation. Assess the complete activity combination and current eligibility. A licence for one role should not be treated as blanket permission for every operation at that address.
posts.body:
Build an activity matrix

List activities down the page and entities and premises across it. Record manufacturing, wholesale, retail, storage, import or other roles only where they occur. This makes it easier to see whether the question is several activities at one site or a network of separate sites.

Resolve route conflicts before filing

Different KoBs can have different eligibility and document requirements. If one selected activity requires Central licensing, do not rely on the ordinary registration band for the others to settle the combined application. Check the relevant current rows and the live FoSCoS treatment of the combination. Read the eligibility table.

Describe products and operations consistently

The application should connect the selected activities to the actual products and process. A wholesaler adding repacking changes how food is handled and introduces manufacturing-related responsibilities. Keep premises evidence, equipment, hygiene arrangements and product scope coherent with the proposed endorsements.

Distinguish an added activity from another premises

Adding a KoB at an existing site is not the same as authorising a new factory or warehouse. Where legal entities differ, establish who needs which authorisation. The fact that two businesses share an address or owner does not settle their regulatory responsibilities. Read the multi-location guide.

Maintain a controlled scope register

Record the certificate number, KoBs, products, sites and pending changes. Before entering a new contract, compare its activities with that register. If a modification is required, identify supporting evidence and the point at which the new activity may legally begin. Review the modification process.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A distributor begins dividing bulk spices into retail packs at its warehouse. The activity matrix shows that repacking introduces a different role from distributing sealed products. The business reviews the route, site controls and endorsement changes before presenting the existing distribution licence as sufficient.

Your practical checklist

  • Map activities against entities and premises.
  • Check each relevant KoB row.
  • Resolve the combined route in FoSCoS.
  • Connect products and evidence to every activity.
  • Separate site additions from KoB additions.
  • Keep a current endorsement register.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our Multiple KOB Assessment service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

headings.text: Distinguish an added activity from another premises

faq.q: Can one authorisation contain several KoBs?
faq.a: Assess the eligible activities at the same premises and the appropriate route for their combination.

faq.q: Does one licence cover every business I own?
faq.a: No. Entity, site and activity boundaries still matter.

faq.q: Can I add repacking to distribution?
faq.a: Review the route, evidence and modification needed for the added handling activity.

faq.q: Do several KoBs mean several government fees?
faq.a: Check the live application and applicable fee rules rather than multiplying a generic fee by the number of activities.

faq.q: Can I start while a modification is pending?
faq.a: Establish the operative position for the added activity; a pending request alone is not evidence of endorsement.

posts.title: Multi-State Operations: Head Office Licence and Branch Licences
posts.description: Multi-state food operations need a licensing assessment for the head office and each operating premises
posts.lede: Multi-state food operations need a licensing assessment for the head office and each operating premises. The 2026 table specifies a Central head-office route for businesses operating in two or more states. That authorisation does not replace appropriate factory, kitchen, warehouse or branch authorisations.
posts.body:
Map the network before counting licences

Prepare a list of legal entities, registered or head office, states, kitchens, factories, warehouses and sales premises. Add outsourced sites where another operator is responsible. Distinguish a correspondence office from a food premises, and explain who controls each operation.

Check the head-office criterion

The current Head Office row covers operations in two or more states and specifies Central licensing without a turnover restriction. Apply the rule to the actual business network rather than assuming a single-state company needs this route simply because customers live elsewhere. Read the head-office row.

Assess branches by their own activities

The authorisation for each site depends on its KoB and current criteria. An import-related role, manufacturing site and retail outlet can have different routes. Check special locations and product categories as well as turnover. A head-office certificate is not an operating certificate for every branch. Compare the licensing routes.

Keep a premises register

Record site addresses, operators, certificate numbers, KoBs, products, current status and responsible contacts. Use the register for supplier onboarding, invoice details and platform accounts. New sites should enter the assessment process before opening, while closed sites need their own closure review.

Allocate continuing obligations

Assign responsibility for site hygiene, supervisor coverage, fee checks, applicable returns and modifications. A central compliance team can coordinate the work, but site staff must understand the records and controls. During acquisitions or relocations, reconcile certificates with legal and operational changes instead of updating only the corporate spreadsheet.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A food brand has an office in Delhi, production in Haryana and a warehouse in Maharashtra. It maps each operator and activity, assesses the multi-state head-office route and reviews each operating site separately. Supplier and marketplace records then reference the premises that actually perform the relevant work.

Your practical checklist

  • Create an entity and premises map.
  • Identify the states of actual operations.
  • Assess the Central head-office row.
  • Review each branch by activity and criteria.
  • Maintain certificate and status records.
  • Assign site-specific compliance owners.

Download this preparation checklist

headings.text: Map the network before counting licences
Assess branches by their own activities

faq.q: When is a head-office Central licence relevant?
faq.a: The current table specifies it for food-business operations in two or more states.

faq.q: Does it cover every branch automatically?
faq.a: No. Operating premises still require appropriate authorisations.

faq.q: Do customers in other states make me multi-state?
faq.a: Assess actual operations and the relevant rule; customer geography alone does not describe the premises network.

faq.q: Can outsourced warehouses be ignored?
faq.a: No. Identify their operators and licensing responsibilities.

faq.q: What happens when a branch closes?
faq.a: Review surrender and closure requirements for that authorisation and update network records.

posts.title: How to Modify an FSSAI Licence: Adding Products, Changing Address or Capacity
posts.description: Modify an FSSAI authorisation when a material change affects its approved details or scope
posts.lede: Modify an FSSAI authorisation when a material change affects its approved details or scope. Adding products, changing activities, relocating and changing the legal operator are different questions. Establish the correct route before assuming every change can be handled by editing one field.
posts.body:
Describe the change precisely

Prepare a before-and-after table covering the entity, address, KoBs, product list, process and relevant technical details. Separate a spelling correction from a new operating premises or legal entity. This prevents a routine modification request from concealing a more substantial licensing change.

Check the correct workflow

Use the current FoSCoS modification facility and licensing guidance. The 2026 threshold-transition FAQs describe a specific self-declaration migration process and explain that other modifications continue through existing procedures. Do not apply the threshold-migration concession to an unrelated address or ownership change. Read the transition FAQs.

Adding a product needs a product review

Check classification, ingredients, additives and any prior approval before requesting endorsement. A product list is not a substitute for a compliant formulation. Specialised products can affect the applicable licence route. Review classification and manufacturing eligibility.

Keep evidence and implementation aligned

Prepare the supporting documents relevant to the change. Retain the submitted application, receipt and authority queries. Identify when the changed operation may begin under the applicable procedure; do not treat the submission reference as the revised certificate. After a decision, compare the issued details with the requested changes.

Update the documents used by customers

Once the correct change is established, reconcile invoices, pack business details, marketplace certificates and internal registers. Control old artwork and certificates to prevent conflicting versions from circulating. Keep a dated change record explaining the basis of the decision.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A snack producer adds a supplement-style powder and asks only for product addition. Reviewing its intended use identifies a specialised category and further requirements. The business assesses those questions before changing the endorsed list, avoiding an assumption that a new product name alone resolves compliance.

Your practical checklist

  • Prepare a before-and-after matrix.
  • Identify modification, migration or new-application issues.
  • Review new products before endorsement.
  • Gather change-specific supporting evidence.
  • Track the authority decision and revised details.
  • Reconcile labels, invoices and platform records.

Download this preparation checklist

faq.a: No. Assess the premises change and applicable licensing procedure.

faq.a: The 2026 FAQs describe a specific threshold-migration process; distinguish it from other changes.

faq.a: Assess whether changed business details affect the declarations and control the affected stock.

faq.q: Does submission authorise the new activity?
faq.a: A pending request is not the same as a decision endorsing the changed scope.

posts.title: FSSAI Application Reverted or Rejected? How to Respond
posts.description: A reverted FSSAI application usually requires clarification or correction; rejection is an authority decision that needs a different review
posts.lede: A reverted FSSAI application usually requires clarification or correction; rejection is an authority decision that needs a different review. Open the complete communication, identify its grounds and deadline, and respond with evidence addressing each point.
posts.body:
Read the status and communication together

Save the application reference, status history, query or rejection order and date of receipt. A short dashboard label can omit the reason or deadline. Distinguish an unsubmitted draft, pending payment, clarification request and formal rejection before deciding whether to resubmit or seek review.

Create a point-by-point response

Make a table with the authority’s question, your explanation, supporting attachment and location of the correction. Common application problems include mismatched entity names, wrong premises evidence, unsuitable KoBs or incomplete product documents. Correct the underlying application details as well as the cover letter. Check document consistency.

Treat rejection as a separate decision

Read the reasons and cited provision. Section 31 provides an appeal route for a rejected licence application; the appropriate forum and procedure should be assessed against the actual order and current rules. Do not confuse this with the separate appeal provisions for an improvement notice. Read the Act.

Keep the account secure

Use official FoSCoS access and retain submission acknowledgements. Consultants can prepare evidence, but users should control their account and payment records. Do not share OTPs with an unverified caller promising approval or pay an unofficial account to make a query disappear.

Reconcile the final result

After responding, track whether the authority asks for more evidence or issues a decision. Confirm the actual certificate before starting an activity that requires authorisation. A revised attachment should remain linked to the submitted version so later questions can be answered from a coherent file.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

An application is reverted because the rental document identifies a different floor. The applicant obtains appropriate premises evidence and explains the discrepancy in a query-response table. Uploading a clearer photograph alone would not have resolved the mismatch, so the response fixes the factual issue.

Your practical checklist

  • Save the complete communication and receipt date.
  • Identify the status and response deadline.
  • Map every query to evidence and corrections.
  • Review formal rejection grounds separately.
  • Submit through the official workflow.
  • Keep the acknowledgement and final decision.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our Application Clarification / Resubmission service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

headings.text: Read the status and communication together
Treat rejection as a separate decision

faq.q: Is reverted the same as rejected?
faq.a: No. A clarification request and a formal rejection require different actions.

faq.q: Should I create a new application immediately?
faq.a: First read the existing communication and determine the appropriate correction or review route.

faq.q: Can I appeal rejection?
faq.a: The Act provides a licensing-rejection appeal framework; obtain advice on the particular order and procedure.

faq.q: What if a document is unclear?
faq.a: Replace it with legible evidence and explain any underlying inconsistency.

faq.q: Can someone guarantee approval after a query?
faq.a: No. The competent authority evaluates the application and decides the outcome.

posts.title: Change of Ownership, Partners or Company Name on an FSSAI Licence
posts.description: Changing a company name, partners, ownership or legal constitution can affect an FSSAI authorisation differently
posts.lede: Changing a company name, partners, ownership or legal constitution can affect an FSSAI authorisation differently. Identify whether the same legal entity continues and who will operate the food premises. A transfer following an owner’s death is a specific route, not a general shortcut for every business sale.
posts.body:
Separate name from legal identity

A company renaming itself may remain the same legal person. A proprietorship sold to a company or a change in constitution can create different operator facts. Gather incorporation, partnership, ownership and authorisation documents before selecting a portal action.

Review the actual certificate and arrangement

Compare the current applicant, premises, KoBs and responsible person with the proposed operator. Identify who controls production and stock during the change. Legal documents alone do not show whether the food activity has moved to another premises or whether the new operator requires a fresh assessment.

Do not generalise the death-transfer provision

Official licensing FAQs describe transfer following the holder’s death, supported by a death certificate and legal-heir evidence. That is a particular circumstance. Other acquisitions, partner changes and constitution changes must use the appropriate current procedure. Read the transfer guidance.

Prepare the transition file

Keep the old and new details, effective dates, supporting instruments, board or partner authority and current account communications. Seek clarification where the correct route is uncertain before choosing a convenient field. Track fees, pending returns and authority matters so outstanding obligations are not lost between operators.

Reconcile consumer and commercial information

Review pack business declarations, invoices, website details and platform records against the approved position. Allocate responsibility for old stock and complaints. A company-name change should not cause the manufacturing identity or licence number on packaging to become ambiguous. Read the label licence-number guide.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A proprietor incorporates a company and plans to invoice all future stock through it. The assessment treats this as an operator and constitution question rather than simply correcting the proprietor’s spelling. The transition plan maps the premises, authorisation, existing stock and customer information to the appropriate entity.

Your practical checklist

  • Identify whether the legal entity continues.
  • Compare actual operator and certificate details.
  • Gather constitution and authorisation documents.
  • Assess the specific transfer or modification route.
  • Resolve pending obligations during transition.
  • Review labels, invoices and platform records.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our Change in Constitution / Business Details service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

headings.text: Review the actual certificate and arrangement
Do not generalise the death-transfer provision

faq.q: Is a company name change the same as ownership transfer?
faq.a: No. Determine whether the same legal person continues.

faq.q: Can I transfer a deceased owner’s licence?
faq.a: The licensing framework has a specific legal-heir transfer procedure and evidence requirements.

faq.q: Can that procedure be used for any acquisition?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Assess the particular transaction and current procedure.

faq.q: Do labels need review after a change?
faq.a: Yes, where the responsible business details or authorisation information are affected.

faq.q: Who handles old complaints?
faq.a: Define responsibilities in the transition plan while preserving applicable statutory duties.

posts.title: How to Surrender or Close an FSSAI Licence
posts.description: When a food business permanently closes, address its FSSAI authorisation as well as its premises and tax arrangements
posts.lede: When a food business permanently closes, address its FSSAI authorisation as well as its premises and tax arrangements. The March 2026 licensing amendment requires written notification and surrender within 30 days of closure. Perpetual validity makes a recorded closure process especially important.
posts.body:
Confirm what is closing

Identify the entity, operating premises and specific authorisation. Closing one warehouse is different from closing the company or every site. Decide whether activities have stopped permanently, moved elsewhere or been transferred to another operator. A new location should be assessed separately rather than concealed within a closure request.

Follow the written-notification requirement

The 2026 amendment requires the holder to inform the authority in writing and surrender within 30 days of closure. It also provides that surrender does not entitle the holder to a fee refund. Retain proof of the communication and surrender submission. Read the closure provision.

Reconcile stock and outstanding matters

Record the last production or trading date, remaining food stock, supplier balances, complaints and any authority proceedings. Determine lawful handling of stock, including expiry or recall issues. Closing the account does not erase traceability needs or unresolved obligations.

Use the current official workflow

Check the surrender option and supporting requirements in FoSCoS. Save the account status before and after the request, the acknowledgement and the final recorded position. If the portal prevents a filing, raise a documented official support request and preserve the written closure notice.

Update the operational network

Remove the closed site from active listings and supplier records, tell the responsible internal teams and retain the historical certificate file. Multi-site businesses should keep other sites’ obligations active. For a temporary pause, establish the appropriate regulatory position rather than describing the business as permanently closed.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A distributor closes a small warehouse while retaining a retail outlet. The closure file identifies the warehouse authorisation, stock transfer records and closure date. It records the surrender process for that site while keeping the outlet’s compliance calendar active.

Your practical checklist

  • Identify the exact site and authorisation.
  • Record the permanent closure date.
  • Notify the authority in writing.
  • Surrender within the applicable 30-day period.
  • Retain stock, complaint and obligation records.
  • Remove closed-site details from active channels.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our Licence Surrender / Closure service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

faq.q: Does perpetual validity end automatically on closure?
faq.a: Complete the required notification and surrender process rather than leaving an unused authorisation active.

faq.q: What is the closure deadline?
faq.a: The March 2026 amendment specifies surrender within 30 days of closure.

faq.q: Will surrender refund prepaid fees?
faq.a: The amendment states that surrender does not create a refund entitlement.

faq.q: Does closing one site close every licence?
faq.a: No. Identify the particular authorisation and keep continuing sites compliant.

faq.q: Can I ignore pending notices after closure?
faq.a: No. Preserve records and assess unresolved obligations and proceedings.

posts.title: FSSAI for Retailers, Kirana Stores, Distributors and Wholesalers
posts.description: Retailers, distributors and wholesalers need the appropriate FSSAI authorisation for their food-trading activities and premises
posts.lede: Retailers, distributors and wholesalers need the appropriate FSSAI authorisation for their food-trading activities and premises. The revised 2026 table changes the general turnover bands. Selling sealed food rather than making it does not remove food-business responsibilities.
posts.body:
Choose the trading role accurately

Retail generally involves selling to consumers, while wholesale and distribution describe other positions in the supply chain. Map who buys stock, who invoices the sale and who stores it. A kirana adding bulk repacking or in-store food preparation should assess those added operations separately.

Use current turnover criteria

For the ordinary trading rows, the 2026 table provides registration up to ₹1.5 crore, State licensing above ₹1.5 crore up to ₹50 crore, and Central above ₹50 crore, subject to applicable special conditions. Do not use the old ₹12 lakh registration figure. Review the actual trading rows.

Check premises and stock controls

Prepare the documents required for the selected route and the actual shop or distribution location. Manage damaged packs, expired products, pest control, storage conditions and separation from non-food chemicals. A trading business should be able to identify its supplier and the batches supplied onward.

Verify supplier documents and food information

Check the supplier’s identity, appropriate authorisation, invoice and product labels. A printed licence number alone is insufficient to resolve whether that supplier and product match the transaction. Keep records that make a complaint or recall traceable. Verify licence details; plan traceability.

Watch for activity changes

Imports, private-label commissioning, transport, warehouse operations and e-commerce can create separate questions. The June 2026 licence-condition amendment also distinguishes applicability for particular activities; read the actual conditions rather than imposing a manufacturing checklist on a retailer. Read the amendment.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A kirana selling sealed spice packs begins buying bulk spices and packing them under its own name. The owner reviews the new repacking role, premises controls and labels rather than assuming the existing retail activity covers the expanded model.

Your practical checklist

  • Map retail, wholesale and distribution activities.
  • Use current turnover and special criteria.
  • Prepare premises evidence.
  • Control storage, expiry and damaged products.
  • Verify supplier identities and records.
  • Review repacking, import or online additions.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our Basic FSSAI Registration service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

headings.text: Verify supplier documents and food information

faq.q: Does a kirana need FSSAI authorisation?
faq.a: Assess the appropriate registration or licensing route for its food-trading activity.

faq.q: Do sealed packs remove the requirement?
faq.a: No. Food-trading obligations remain.

faq.q: Is the old ₹12 lakh threshold current?
faq.a: No. Use the revised 2026 eligibility table.

faq.q: Can a retailer pack bulk food under its brand?
faq.a: Assess repacking or other added activities and product-label obligations.

faq.q: What records matter for traders?
faq.a: Supplier, invoice, batch, stock-condition and onward-distribution records help establish traceability.

posts.title: FSSAI for Warehouses, Cold Storage and Transporters
posts.description: Food storage and transport activities have their own FSSAI KoB rows
posts.lede: Food storage and transport activities have their own FSSAI KoB rows. A warehouse, cold-storage facility and food transporter should assess the actual operator, premises and current eligibility. The customer’s food licence does not automatically settle the service provider’s responsibilities.
posts.body:
Map the storage and movement arrangement

Identify the owner of the food, operator of the facility, transporter and parties controlling temperature and loading. Separate ambient storage, controlled-atmosphere storage, cold storage and vehicle operations where the table distinguishes them. Record each operating address and outsourced arrangement.

Check the revised criteria

Use the current storage and transport rows rather than old capacity or vehicle-count guidance copied from earlier tables. The 2026 eligibility PDF provides the route and fees by activity. Read special location and mixed-activity conditions where applicable. Current storage and transport eligibility.

Design controls around the food

Define receiving checks, temperature requirements, incompatible goods, cleaning and pest controls. Refrigeration set points must fit the products actually stored; one generic cold-room temperature does not establish compliance for every food. Preserve handling instructions and identify who investigates temperature excursions.

Keep traceable movement records

Record incoming and outgoing batches, quantities, customers, dates and relevant vehicle or temperature information. A recall requires a usable link between stock and destinations, not merely a pile of invoices. Establish how returned, damaged or expired goods are segregated and prevented from re-entering sale.

Review added processing activities

Opening packs, repacking, relabelling or preparing products changes the activity assessment. Assess such changes before presenting them as incidental warehousing. Contract documents should allocate responsibilities clearly, while recognising that applicable statutory duties are not removed simply by a private agreement. Review repacking and relabelling.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A fulfilment warehouse stores dry snacks and refrigerated desserts for several brands. It establishes product-specific receiving and storage controls, batch-location records and dispatch responsibilities. When a customer requests local relabelling, the operator treats it as an added compliance question instead of an ordinary picking instruction.

Your practical checklist

  • Identify facility and transporter operators.
  • Distinguish the actual storage types.
  • Check current KoB rows.
  • Set product-specific storage and movement controls.
  • Maintain batch and destination records.
  • Assess repacking or relabelling requests separately.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our State FSSAI Licence – New service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

faq.a: Assess the warehouse operator’s own activities and authorisation needs.

faq.q: Do old storage-capacity thresholds still apply?
faq.a: Use the revised 2026 table for the current route assessment.

faq.q: Is cold storage just ordinary storage?
faq.a: Review the specific activity row and product handling requirements.

faq.q: Can food travel with other goods?
faq.a: Assess contamination, segregation and product-condition risks in the actual transport arrangement.

faq.q: What if we apply new labels?
faq.a: Review whether the task creates a relabelling or other regulated activity.

posts.title: FSSAI for Repackers and Relabellers
posts.description: Repacking food and commissioning manufacture under your brand are different regulatory roles
posts.lede: Repacking food and commissioning manufacture under your brand are different regulatory roles. Assess Repacker or Relabeller using the actual production arrangement, not the appearance of the finished pack. The correct KoB, product scope and responsibility information should agree.
posts.body:
Understand the two arrangements

A repacker handles food by dividing or packing it from bulk into different packages. A relabeller commonly has products manufactured by a third party under its own brand arrangement. Opening food locally introduces different facility and hygiene facts from buying finished packs from a contract factory. Read the activity descriptions.

Assess the full licensing route

Check the revised 2026 criteria for the actual activity and products. Specialised product requirements can override general turnover assumptions. A brand that has no factory may still have food-business licensing duties. Review the commissioned products and their manufacturing sites before filing.

Obtain manufacturer and product evidence

For contract production, establish the manufacturer’s entity, site, relevant authorisation and endorsed product capability. Collect the recipe, specifications and supporting agreement or consent required by the live application. A generic letter from a factory does not establish the compliance of every proposed product.

Align pack responsibilities

The label should correctly identify responsible businesses and applicable licence numbers. The brand owner and different manufacturer or packer can require distinct declarations. Avoid printing only whichever number fits the available space. Read licence-number declarations; review private-label responsibilities.

Maintain manufacturing-related obligations

Repacking and relabelling can fall within annual-return and testing frameworks identified in official guidance. Assess applicability against your role and endorsed products, and arrange access to batch and test records from the manufacturer. Outsourcing production should not make product evidence inaccessible. Annual-return guidance; testing-report guidance.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A spice brand receives finished pouches from a factory and initially applies as a retailer. Its production agreement leads to a relabeller assessment. Later, when it starts filling jars from bulk stock itself, the added physical handling creates a repacking and premises review.

Your practical checklist

  • Describe whether food is opened locally.
  • Identify the contract manufacturer and site.
  • Check activity and specialised-product criteria.
  • Prepare product specifications and agreements.
  • Align responsible-business label declarations.
  • Assess returns, testing and batch-record access.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our Multiple KOB Assessment service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

faq.q: Are repacker and relabeller interchangeable?
faq.a: No. Assess the physical handling and commissioned-production arrangement.

faq.q: Can a brand without a factory have licensing duties?
faq.a: Yes. Its own role in the food business still needs assessment.

faq.q: Whose number goes on a private-label pack?
faq.a: Apply the relevant brand-owner and manufacturer/packer declaration rules.

faq.q: Do relabellers need D1 assessment?
faq.a: Yes. Official return guidance includes relevant relabeller activities.

faq.q: Can manufacturer records be outsourced too?
faq.a: Arrange access and clear responsibility; outsourcing should not leave required evidence unavailable.

posts.title: FSSAI for Street Food Vendors, Hawkers and Seasonal Businesses
posts.description: Street vendors and hawkers should check the applicable registration position, hygiene requirements and local permissions
posts.lede: Street vendors and hawkers should check the applicable registration position, hygiene requirements and local permissions. The 2026 licensing amendment recognises street vendors registered under the Street Vendors Act, 2014 as deemed registered under the food framework, while keeping hygiene obligations.
posts.body:
Identify the vendor’s actual status

Record whether the business is a mobile hawker, a fixed stall, an occasional event seller or another food-service model. Check the actual street-vendor registration and location permissions. Selling at a seasonal market does not automatically establish registration under the Street Vendors Act.

Understand deemed registration

The March 2026 amendment provides deemed registration for street vendors registered under the 2014 Act. Keep evidence that establishes the relevant status. Do not turn that specific rule into a claim that all street food or all temporary businesses are exempt. Read the amendment.

Check the route and fee where an application is needed

Use the current KoB table and official workflow for the actual business. The revised table records a registration-fee waiver for listed hawkers, with the stated earlier implementation date. A fee waiver is different from exemption from hygiene or permission to select an inaccurate KoB. Review hawker eligibility.

Control practical food-safety risks

Protect food from dust, pests and contamination; use safe water and appropriate utensils; plan hand hygiene and waste disposal. Separate raw and ready-to-eat food and manage holding conditions. A small mobile setup needs workable controls that staff can apply throughout service.

Prepare for seasonal and location changes

Check temporary-site arrangements, local permissions and any change in operator or activity. Keep supplier and purchase records and a way to handle customer complaints. A seasonal operation should record opening and closure decisions rather than assume the calendar removes its obligations.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A vendor has a town-vending registration and checks whether it establishes the deemed-registration position. A neighbouring pop-up stall has only an event organiser’s receipt, so it assesses its own route. Both vendors still plan safe water, food protection and waste controls.

Your practical checklist

  • Record vendor type and operating location.
  • Check genuine Street Vendors Act registration.
  • Assess deemed registration or application route.
  • Verify any applicable fee waiver.
  • Prepare water, hygiene and holding controls.
  • Check seasonal and local-permission arrangements.

posts.title: Tatkal FSSAI Licence and Registration: Who Qualifies?
posts.description: Tatkal is an official instant-issuance facility for specified eligible food-business activities, subject to digital verification and exclusions
posts.lede: Tatkal is an official instant-issuance facility for specified eligible food-business activities, subject to digital verification and exclusions. It is not a universal fast-track route for every manufacturer or a service through which a consultant can guarantee approval.
posts.body:
Check the eligible activity list

Official FAQs include specified trading, storage, transport, importer, merchant-exporter and listed petty-business activities. Confirm the precise KoB in the live application and FAQ rather than assuming any business can apply because its documents are ready. Read the instant-issuance FAQs.

Check applicant and premises eligibility

The FAQ excludes applicants who already hold a valid authorisation at the same premises, applicants with suspended authorisations, those cancelled within the specified recent period and businesses outside the listed KoBs. Review the exact conditions before starting; Tatkal is not a workaround for a suspension.

Prepare digital-verification evidence

The FAQ sets out GST/Aadhaar or PAN/Aadhaar verification according to applicant and route, with particular treatment for listed petty activities. It also requires front-facing premises photographs showing the address and applicant. Read the route-specific evidence rather than treating identity numbers alone as the complete file.

Keep the declarations accurate

The rapid workflow relies on the truth of the applicant’s information. Do not select Retailer to obtain a faster certificate for an actual manufacturing operation. Review official fees at the payment stage and retain the issued record. Do not pay an unofficial expedited-service account represented as FSSAI.

Apply continuing obligations

The current FAQ confirms that perpetual validity and revised turnover criteria also apply to Tatkal authorisations. Instant issuance does not remove annual-fee, return, hygiene or scope requirements. Compare the issued details with the actual activity and resolve discrepancies. Read the validity explanation.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A distributor checks the instant-issuance list and prepares the required verification and premises photographs. A manufacturer selling direct asks to use the same route but finds that its actual manufacturing activity needs a separate eligibility review. The two businesses do not change their KoBs just to share the faster workflow.

Your practical checklist

  • Confirm the actual KoB is listed.
  • Read applicant and authorisation exclusions.
  • Prepare route-specific digital verification.
  • Take the required accurate premises photographs.
  • Review declarations and official payment.
  • Verify the issued scope and continuing duties.

Download this preparation checklist

For help applying this review to your business, explore our Basic FSSAI Registration service. Bring the documents described above so the consultation can focus on the decisions still unresolved.

faq.a: The current official FAQ says the revised validity framework applies.

faq.a: No. Eligibility, verification and official processing determine the result.

posts.title: How to Check Whether an FSSAI Licence Number Is Valid
posts.description: Verify an FSSAI number through the official system and compare the returned business details with the actual supplier or premises
posts.lede: Verify an FSSAI number through the official system and compare the returned business details with the actual supplier or premises. A plausible-looking number printed on a pack is not enough: entity, address, status and scope must fit the transaction.
posts.body:
Use the official search

Open FoSCoS and use the current public verification or business-search facility. Enter the number carefully, without confusing an application reference with the issued authorisation number. Save the result and date for supplier-review records. Official FoSCoS portal.

Compare the identity and location

Check the name and address against the pack, invoice and supplier documents. Differences can reflect separate brand-owner and manufacturing entities, but the explanation should be coherent. An unrelated certificate cannot validate a food business simply because its status is active.

Assess status and scope

Review the available authorisation status and relevant business or product details. If scope information is insufficient, obtain the current certificate and supporting product evidence from the supplier. A verification result does not establish the safety of a particular batch or approve a marketing claim.

Interpret dates under the current framework

The 2026 perpetual-validity change means an old expiry-only checklist can be misleading. Review the actual certificate and account status, including legacy-transition questions. Suspension and cancellation still matter even where an ordinary future expiry date is absent. Understand current validity.

Investigate discrepancies systematically

Ask the supplier for an explanation and the current issued record. Preserve pack photographs, invoice details and the verification result. If the record cannot be reconciled, use official support or the relevant authority channel. Do not accuse a business of fraud solely because one search attempt fails or a portal is temporarily unavailable.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A retailer finds that a pack’s brand-owner number corresponds to the marketing company, while a second number identifies the factory. It compares both declarations with the supplier file instead of expecting one entity to perform every role. An unrelated number would remain an unresolved discrepancy.

Your practical checklist

  • Use the official verification facility.
  • Enter the issued number accurately.
  • Compare entity and premises details.
  • Check current status and relevant scope.
  • Interpret legacy dates carefully.
  • Record and investigate discrepancies.

faq.a: No. Verify it and compare the business details and relevant scope.

faq.a: No. Batch safety, formulation and claims require separate evidence.

faq.q: Why are there two numbers on a pack?
faq.a: Applicable brand-owner and manufacturer or packer declarations can involve different responsible businesses.

faq.q: What if the portal returns no result?
faq.a: Recheck the input, obtain the certificate and use official support before drawing a conclusion.

faq.q: Should I rely only on expiry dates?
faq.a: No. Review current status and the 2026 validity framework.

posts.title: Penalty for Running a Food Business Without an FSSAI Licence
posts.description: Operating a food business without the required FSSAI licence can attract prosecution under section 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act
posts.lede: Operating a food business without the required FSSAI licence can attract prosecution under section 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act. The applicable provision depends on the business and authorisation requirement; small-business registration issues should not be described with a single universal penalty.
posts.body:
Establish which authorisation is required

Start with the actual activity, premises and current eligibility. Section 31 contains the licensing requirement and treatment of petty food businesses. The revised 2026 bands can change the route, while special KoB rows still apply. Read sections 31 and 63; current eligibility.

Understand the section 63 maximum

The Act’s section 63 concerns a person required to obtain a licence who conducts the stated food activities without one, except the exemption addressed through section 31(2). It provides imprisonment up to six months and a fine up to ₹5 lakh. These are statutory maxima, not an automatic bill for every registration lapse. Read the operative law and facts before applying them.

Other offences are separate

Unsafe food, misbranding, misleading advertising, obstruction and false information have their own provisions. Obtaining an authorisation later does not automatically erase earlier conduct. Conversely, a portal upload problem does not itself establish every element of an offence. Keep legal classification separate from general warnings.

Respond to an actual notice carefully

Preserve the notice, certificate history, application evidence, operating dates and current activity details. Do not backdate records or make unsupported admissions. Obtain professional advice on the allegations, deadline and appropriate response, while addressing immediate food-safety issues. Read the notice-response guide.

Correct the authorisation position

Assess the proper application or restoration route, resolve outstanding obligations and verify active status before undertaking activities requiring authorisation. The current perpetual-validity framework also prohibits operation during suspension. A pending application or payment receipt is not the issued certificate.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A trader receives a notice alleging operation without a licence. Its file establishes the actual activity, turnover period and historical authorisation record. The response assesses the applicable route and dates rather than accepting a generic online claim that every small food seller automatically faces the same punishment.

Your practical checklist

  • Identify the required route and relevant period.
  • Read the actual statutory allegation.
  • Treat maximum penalties as maxima.
  • Preserve applications and certificate history.
  • Obtain advice on a real notice.
  • Resolve and verify the authorisation position.

faq.a: No. Section 63 states a maximum and has a defined licensing scope.

faq.q: Can imprisonment apply?
faq.a: The cited provision includes imprisonment, subject to the offence and legal process.

faq.q: Does later licensing erase earlier conduct?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Assess the actual facts and proceedings.

faq.q: Can I operate on a payment receipt?
faq.a: A receipt is not the same as an issued authorisation.

faq.q: What if my licence is suspended?
faq.a: The amended validity provision prohibits food business during suspension; assess restoration and the actual grounds.

posts.title: FSSAI Annual Return (Form D-1): Who Must File and By When
posts.description: Form D1 applies to specified licensed manufacturing and importing activities, including relevant repackers, relabellers and exporter-manufacturers
posts.lede: Form D1 applies to specified licensed manufacturing and importing activities, including relevant repackers, relabellers and exporter-manufacturers. It is not a universal return for every restaurant or retailer. The baseline deadline is 31 May for the preceding financial year; check year-specific directions before filing.
posts.body:
Check applicability from the actual KoB

Official FAQs describe licensed manufacturers, including repacking and relabelling arrangements, and importers within the D1 framework. Exporter-manufacturers are also covered by the stated later extension. Compare your certificate and activity with the requirement, rather than assuming every authorisation holder files the same return. Read the annual-return FAQs.

Identify the reporting year

Reconcile production or importing records for the preceding financial year. The baseline deadline is 31 May, but any current extension or special direction must be checked for that particular year. Do not carry an extension from one year into another or use a deadline from a social-media message without its official order.

Prepare product and quantity records

Work from actual product, production, import and transaction records. Use the units and fields requested in the live FoSCoS form. Resolve mismatches with stock and accounting records before submission. A nil-activity situation needs an applicability and filing review, rather than invented quantities or an unsupported assumption that no return is required.

Review late filing under current instructions

The official baseline FAQ states ₹100 per day for late submission. Current account calculations, applicable caps or specific directions need their own check. The March 2026 validity amendment also links non-submission of an applicable return to deemed suspension. Keep the penalty calculation and status issue separate. Read the amended validity provision.

Keep proof and improve the next cycle

File through the official workflow and retain the submitted data, acknowledgement and payment evidence where relevant. Record who prepared and checked the figures. Update production and import records during the year so the next return does not become a reconstruction from invoices alone.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A relabeller commissions snack manufacture at two factories. It gathers actual production and product records under the arrangement, checks return applicability and reconciles the reporting units before filing. The factories’ own records do not automatically establish that the brand’s separate filing obligations are complete.

Your practical checklist

  • Check the licensed activities and D1 applicability.
  • Confirm reporting year and any official extension.
  • Reconcile quantities and requested units.
  • Review nil activity and outstanding periods.
  • Check late-fee and suspension implications.
  • Retain submission and payment acknowledgements.

posts.title: FSSAI Licence for Tiffin Services, Mess and Canteens
posts.description: A tiffin service, mess and canteen should select the KoB that matches how meals are prepared and supplied
posts.lede: A tiffin service, mess and canteen should select the KoB that matches how meals are prepared and supplied. The 2026 table distinguishes home-based canteens or dabbawalas, clubs and canteens, and caterers. Do not apply one turnover answer to all three models.
posts.body:
Describe the meal-service arrangement

Record the kitchen, operator, customers and service locations. Daily subscriptions from a home kitchen differ from an institutional canteen or organised event catering. A mess serving residents may share facilities with a hostel, but the responsible food-business operator still needs identification.

Read the relevant 2026 row

Home-based canteens/dabbawalas and clubs/canteens have their own eligibility rows. The revised table lists registration up to ₹1.5 crore and a State route above that band for those rows; do not invent a generic Central turnover row where none is shown. Caterers have a separate State/Central pattern. Check the exact meal-service row.

Prepare the premises and operator file

Use the actual kitchen and supporting documents for the selected route. If a hostel or institution engages a contractor, map the contractor and facility responsibilities. Neither the institution’s registration nor a commercial agreement alone settles every food-business authorisation question.

Control preparation and delivery

Plan safe water, ingredient storage, cooking, holding, cleaning and dispatch. Reusable containers require a workable cleaning and return arrangement. For subscriptions, record customer restrictions and communicate allergen-related information accurately rather than making unsupported allergen-free promises.

Review expansion before accepting new work

A service moving from home lunches to institutional catering, opening another kitchen or selling packaged snacks should revisit its KoB and premises assessment. Keep the authorised scope, menu representations and operating controls aligned. Read the catering guide and prepare an FSMS plan.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A home lunch service wins a contract to operate a college canteen and provide event catering. It assesses the new institutional site and catering role instead of presenting its original home-kitchen registration as covering every arrangement. The meal-handling plan also expands to transport and event holding.

Your practical checklist

  • Map operator, kitchen and service locations.
  • Distinguish dabbawala, canteen and catering models.
  • Read the exact current eligibility row.
  • Prepare premises and contract evidence.
  • Control food holding, containers and delivery.
  • Review new sites and added packaged products.

posts.title: FSSAI Labelling Requirements: A Complete Guide for Packaged Food Brands
posts.description: Review Indian packaged-food labels with a declaration checklist, annotated illustration, artwork workflow and effective-date guidance for 2026–2027.
posts.lede: A compliant food label starts with the correct product identity, accurate formulation information and the declarations applicable to that product and pack. Review FSSAI labelling rules together with relevant Legal Metrology requirements before approving the artwork for print.
posts.body:
Which labelling rules should a food brand check?

The Labelling and Display Regulations, 2020 address packaged-food labels and certain display information. Read the current compilation alongside later amendments and directions, plus any specialised product rules. FSSAI labelling compendium.

The Department of Consumer Affairs separately explains packaged-commodity declarations, including net quantity, retail price and consumer-care information. A food label therefore needs review across both areas. Official Legal Metrology overview.

Begin the review by recording the exact product and pack. A retail pouch, a non-retail container and a specialised nutrition product may raise different questions. Do not take a checklist prepared for one product and silently apply it to another.

Create a source list with a review date. Note the relevant regulation, amendments, product standard and any operative direction. Where a requirement changes, record when it becomes applicable to your planned artwork. This prevents a draft proposal or a future amendment from being mistaken for today's rule.

Mandatory declarations: a retail-pack checklist

For an ordinary pre-packaged retail food, assess the applicable declarations below and any exemptions or additional category rules. This is a review map, not a claim that every row appears identically on every pack. See regulation 5 and related provisions.

Declaration areaReview question
Food nameDoes the name identify what the product actually is?
Ingredients and additivesDoes the declaration reflect the formulation and relevant component information?
AllergensHave the relevant ingredients and cross-contact questions been assessed?
Nutrition informationAre the applicable nutrients, units, bases and serving details consistent?
Vegetarian/non-vegetarian declarationIs the applicable symbol used with the required presentation?
Business details and licence informationAre the responsible entities and applicable FSSAI details correctly identified?
Batch and datesCan the printed pack be traced to the product's actual coding records?
Storage, use and special declarationsDoes the product need instructions or category-specific statements?
Quantity, price and consumer careHave applicable Legal Metrology declarations been reviewed?
Imported-food informationHave origin, importer and applicable import requirements been checked?

For each row, record “included,” “conditional,” “exemption assessed” or “action required.” Retain the reasoning behind an exemption. A blank space on artwork should not be the only evidence that someone considered the requirement.

Download the pre-print review worksheet

Use the product's true identity as the starting point

FSSAI's labelling FAQ explains that the food's prescribed, common or descriptive name must convey its nature. A brand or fanciful name may accompany it within the applicable conditions. Official FAQ on the name of food.

Give the designer a regulatory naming brief before artwork begins. Include the proposed descriptive name, the product classification and the assumptions underlying both. If the formulation changes during development, review the naming brief again.

Hypothetical example

A brand develops “Morning Crunch,” a name that could describe several different foods. The naming review asks the team to identify the actual product beneath the brand name. A clear descriptive name makes the pack easier to assess and helps the designer allocate space before decorative copy is finalised.

Review pictures alongside words. An image of a particular fruit or grain can influence the consumer's understanding of the composition. Ask the team what evidence supports the visual emphasis and whether any associated declaration question needs examination.

Build ingredients, allergens and nutrition from reliable inputs

Prepare one controlled formulation record for each SKU. Include the components of compound ingredients, supplier specifications and the assumptions used to develop the label. Ask suppliers for clarification where a proprietary blend name conceals information the reviewer needs.

Ingredient order follows the formulation at manufacture. Relevant allergenic ingredients require the applicable separate declaration; the rules include exemptions and conditions that need product-level review. Review the ingredient and allergen provisions.

A useful ingredient review tracks the item used, its supplier name, its descriptive identity, its components and any unresolved declaration issue. This lets the reviewer reconcile the recipe with the label without guessing what a trade name means.

For nutrition, record the evidence source, the product tested or calculated, the reporting units and the basis of the label values. Check whether the report relates to the finished formulation and serving assumptions. Avoid transferring a table from a supplier's raw material onto a finished food pack.

Run an independent arithmetic check before print approval. Look for accidental swaps between milligrams and grams, values reported per serving but headed per 100 g, and changes to serving size that were not reflected elsewhere. Those checks are practical quality controls, rather than a prescribed testing method for every product.

Review dates, coding and storage as an operating system

The current labelling text provides for manufacture or packing and expiry/use-by declarations, with best-before information optional or additional, subject to applicable exceptions. Review the product's date-marking rule. Read regulation 5(10).

Separate the fixed artwork from the information printed during production. Ask where the batch and dates will appear, how the printer applies them and whether the location remains readable after packing. A compliant design concept still needs a workable production method.

Confirm the storage statements with the team responsible for the product's shelf-life assessment. The artwork reviewer needs to understand the assumptions behind the chosen wording. If the product is sensitive after opening, review that use scenario as part of the brief.

Hypothetical example

A refrigerated product has attractive artwork but no reserved coding area. The pre-print review asks the production team to demonstrate where the code will be placed and how it will be read on the finished pack. This catches a production-design gap before the full packaging order.

Check the entities, licence details and commercial declarations

Make a responsibility map for the brand owner, manufacturer, packer, marketer and importer where relevant. Compare it with the business arrangements and current authorisations. The label should be reviewed against that map, rather than copied from a competitor's pack.

Ask the commercial team to provide the intended pack quantity and pricing information. Confirm how consumer enquiries will be received and handled. Put these inputs through the relevant Legal Metrology review instead of treating them as decorative text added at the end.

A change of manufacturer, packer or importer should trigger a label review. Keep those business changes in the same change-control process as ingredient substitutions and pack-size changes. That helps prevent artwork from becoming detached from the actual supply chain.

Understand the 2026 amendment and its future effective date

The amendment notified on 24 March 2026 is stated to come into force on 1 July 2027. It addresses areas including infant-nutrition RDA information, certain nutrition exemptions and non-retail container declarations. Do not label those future provisions as already mandatory in October 2026. Read the 2026 Gazette amendment.

For a packaging project, put the anticipated manufacture and artwork-use periods into the brief. Ask whether the packaging order may extend across an effective-date boundary. The answer can affect the change plan even when the current artwork is being reviewed today.

Use a simple change register: source, publication date, effective date, affected SKU, action and owner. Check later directions before a production decision. The official regulations directory is the place to begin that source review.

Review promotional claims across the whole pack

A declaration checklist does not settle claims such as “natural,” “high protein” or a health benefit. Give promotional wording its own review against the formula and evidence. The food-claims guide explains the questions to ask.

FSSAI's May 2025 advisory asks food businesses to discontinue “100%” claims on labels and promotional material because of misleading implications. Identify this as an advisory and assess the actual wording in context. Read the direct advisory.

Keep an inventory of claims on the front, back, side panels, website images and product descriptions. If the pack changes, update the sales material too. A print correction alone may leave the old statement visible to customers elsewhere.

A practical artwork sign-off process

  1. Freeze the review inputs. Identify the formulation, specifications, product classification and artwork version.
  2. Run the declaration review. Use the applicable rules and record conditional requirements or exemptions.
  3. Review claims and visuals. Assess the consumer message alongside supporting evidence.
  4. Review the actual dieline. Check legibility, folds, seals and coding space on the final layout.
  5. Reconcile the final proof. Compare the printer's proof with the corrected version before approving production.
  6. Archive the decision. Retain the reviewed file, corrections and named sign-off.

posts.title: Mandatory Label Declarations for Packaged Food in India (Checklist)
posts.description: A packaged-food label in India needs a coordinated set of food, business, traceability and commercial declarations
posts.lede: A packaged-food label in India needs a coordinated set of food, business, traceability and commercial declarations. The exact checklist depends on the category and pack. Review FSSAI requirements alongside Legal Metrology and specialised rules before approving artwork.
posts.body:
Start with the product and sale format

Identify the legal food name, recipe, category, retail or non-retail format, local manufacture or import, and any specialised regime. A generic checklist for a retail snack cannot establish the complete requirements for infant food, supplements or a bulk transport container.

Build the declaration matrix

Review areaTypical information to assess
Food identityName, ingredients, additive declarations and allergen information
Nutrition and presentationRequired nutrition information, serving basis, applicable symbols and claims
Responsible businessesRelevant names, addresses, FSSAI logo and licence numbers
Traceability and useBatch or lot, manufacture/packing, expiry/use-by, storage and instructions
Commercial detailsNet quantity, MRP including taxes, consumer-care details and applicable unit sale price

Use the actual provisions and exceptions when converting this matrix into copy. Labelling and Display Regulations; Legal Metrology overview.

Check where and how information appears

Mandatory content must be legible and meet relevant placement, language and size requirements. A complete spreadsheet does not establish that a crowded label works at actual print size. Review the principal display panel, contrast, folds and seams, and variable coding areas.

Keep imported and specialised requirements separate

Imported products need the applicable importer and country-of-origin assessment. Supplement and other specialised labels can require additional warnings or category statements. Do not delete these because a competitor’s pack appears simpler. Read supplement declarations.

Control versions before print

Assign a source and owner to every declaration. Check the final recipe against ingredient and allergen copy, the report against nutrition values, and the issued certificate against business details. The March 2026 amendment has provisions effective in July 2027; record timing before changing current copy. Read the dated amendment.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A snack pouch contains all headings but uses the factory address from an old production agreement. The review checks the manufacturing site and responsible businesses against the current certificate, then rechecks the finished proof. Completeness and factual accuracy are separate review tasks.

Your practical checklist

  • Confirm category and retail format.
  • Prepare food and nutrition declarations.
  • Verify responsible-business details.
  • Plan batch, date and storage information.
  • Review Legal Metrology requirements.
  • Approve legibility at actual pack size.

posts.title: 12 Label Mistakes That Get Food Products Into Trouble
posts.description: Food-label errors often begin with an incorrect product assumption or outdated source data
posts.lede: Food-label errors often begin with an incorrect product assumption or outdated source data. Check the recipe, category and business details before reviewing typography. The following 12 mistakes are practical review points, not a claim that every example has led to an enforcement case.
posts.body:
Six mistakes in the underlying information

  1. Using a marketing name without a suitable food identity.
  2. Copying another SKU’s ingredient list.
  3. Missing components of a compound ingredient.
  4. Declaring an additive without checking its actual function and permission.
  5. Missing allergens from a premix or flavour carrier.
  6. Using nutrition values from an outdated formulation.

These issues require formulation and supplier evidence, not just design changes. Read the ingredient and nutrition provisions.

Six mistakes in presentation and control

  1. Choosing the old non-vegetarian symbol.
  2. Printing an unrelated or outdated licence number.
  3. Using an unsupported high-protein or sugar claim.
  4. Treating best-before as a substitute for all required date marking.
  5. Omitting applicable net-quantity, MRP or consumer-care information.
  6. Approving a screen image without checking the actual-size proof.

Each issue should be assessed against the relevant provision and product facts. Claim criteria; commercial declarations.

Review linked consequences

One recipe change can affect the name, ingredients, allergens, nutrition, claim and symbol assessment. Treating each text box as independent makes it easy to fix one error while preserving another. Build a change checklist that follows the data through every affected declaration.

Classify defects before deciding on stock

Separate a drafting error found before print from a problem already present on distributed packs. For existing stock, assess the exact defect, safety implications and permissible corrective route. A sticker is not a universal remedy, and an attractive reprint does not address food already in the market.

Create a repeatable approval record

Keep the formula version, supplier specifications, reports, certificate details, reviewed artwork and final print proof together. Record unresolved issues and who closed them. Where a real notice or complaint exists, preserve that evidence and assess it separately from an internal artwork checklist.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A cookie brand changes chocolate suppliers. The artwork team updates the flavour name but leaves the previous compound-ingredient details and allergen assessment. A coordinated review catches the linked changes before the print run, without relying on a visual comparison alone.

Your practical checklist

  • Check identity and ingredient source data.
  • Review compound ingredients and additives.
  • Reconcile allergens and nutrition.
  • Verify symbols and licence information.
  • Assess dates and commercial declarations.
  • Keep a final actual-size approval record.

posts.title: How to Write a Statement of Ingredients the FSSAI Way (Order, Percentages, Compound Ingredients)
posts.description: Write the ingredient list from the actual manufacturing formula, normally in descending order by weight at the time of manufacture
posts.lede: Write the ingredient list from the actual manufacturing formula, normally in descending order by weight at the time of manufacture. Compound ingredients, highlighted ingredients, additives and water need additional checks. A supplier’s marketing description is not a complete ingredient specification.
posts.body:
Start from the controlled formula

List each input, its quantity and relevant components. Use the point of manufacture for ordering rather than ranking ingredients by taste, nutrition or their position after moisture loss. Record permitted ingredient names and assess any specific exceptions before drafting the list. Read ingredient-list requirements.

Break down compound ingredients

A chocolate filling, seasoning or premix may itself contain several ingredients. The regulations allow the prescribed bracketed presentation or a suitable declaration of components as individual ingredients. The below-5% compound-ingredient provision has an exception for additives serving a technological function in the final food; it is not permission to ignore every component or separate allergen duties.

Review quantities of emphasised ingredients

Where an ingredient is emphasised through words, pictures or another relevant trigger, assess the required percentage declaration and its exceptions. A large almond photograph can create a question even if the ingredient name appears only once. Keep the quantity calculation linked to the actual recipe.

Check additives, water and component sources

Determine the functional class and specific name or INS declaration for applicable additives. Review added-water treatment under the stated rules. Obtain component and carrier details from suppliers where needed; a proprietary supplier blend does not remove the finished-product manufacturer’s declaration questions.

Reconcile the list with other copy

Check the food name, allergen statement, vegetarian assessment and claims against the final list. Keep the approved wording tied to a recipe version, and assess changes in premix supplier or concentration before reuse. Additive declarations and allergen review complete related tasks.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A bakery uses a cocoa filling described on the purchase invoice only as chocolate paste. It obtains the actual composition, prepares the appropriate compound-ingredient declaration and reviews milk and soy sources. The invoice name alone would not have supported a complete label.

Your practical checklist

  • Use the manufacturing formula and input weights.
  • Obtain compound-ingredient specifications.
  • Check highlighted-ingredient percentages.
  • Review additives, carriers and water.
  • Reconcile allergen and claim information.
  • Record recipe and wording versions.

faq.a: The ordinary rule uses descending weight at the time of manufacture; assess the relevant exceptions.

faq.a: Review the compound-ingredient declaration rules and supplier composition.

faq.a: No. The provision has qualifications and does not erase separate applicable declarations.

faq.q: Do pictures affect percentage declarations?
faq.a: Emphasising an ingredient through presentation can trigger an assessment.

faq.q: Who supplies the component details?
faq.a: Obtain reliable specifications from the supplier and verify them against the actual input.

posts.title: Declaring Food Additives on a Label: Class Titles and INS Numbers
posts.description: An additive label declaration generally combines the functional class with its specific name or recognised INS number
posts.lede: An additive label declaration generally combines the functional class with its specific name or recognised INS number. The declaration must describe an additive actually present and used appropriately. An INS number identifies a substance; it does not establish permission in every food.
posts.body:
Separate permission from declaration

First identify the food category and applicable additive entry, level and notes. Only then draft the label. A correct-looking INS declaration cannot legalise an additive that is not permitted in the product. Read category-specific additive permissions.

Identify the actual technological function

Establish whether the ingredient functions as an acidity regulator, preservative, stabiliser, emulsifier or another applicable class in the finished product. Use the actual role and prescribed terminology rather than whichever class sounds reassuring. The Labelling and Display rules require the class together with the name or recognised INS identifier. Read additive declarations.

Read supplier premix specifications

Seasonings, fillings and colours may introduce several additives or carriers. Check their identities, concentrations and functions. A trade name such as flavour blend or texture system is insufficient to determine every applicable declaration or carry-over question.

Assess carry-over and processing aids carefully

The additive framework has conditions for carry-over. Establish the source, amount and whether a technological function remains in the final food. Do not omit an additive solely because it arrived through another ingredient. Processing-aid treatment also requires the actual substance and use to fit the relevant provision. Read the additive framework.

Check the final recipe and artwork together

Record the decision for each additive and its final wording. Recheck the list when the supplier, dose or food category changes. Keep nutrition and allergen implications in the same review where relevant, without treating additive declarations as an isolated label-design task.

A worked example

Hypothetical example

A drink manufacturer receives a preservative through a fruit preparation. It calculates the contribution and reviews the function in the finished drink before deciding on the label. The supplier’s ingredient list is evidence, but the final-product assessment determines the applicable declaration.

Your practical checklist

  • Identify substance and recognised identifier.
  • Confirm category permission and relevant level.
  • Determine the finished-product function.
  • Review premix contribution and carry-over.
  • Draft class plus name or INS wording.
  • Retain the formulation and label decision.

faq.q: Is an INS number proof of permission?
faq.a: No. Permission depends on the category, conditions and level.

faq.q: Can I declare only the number?
faq.a: Review the required functional-class plus name or INS presentation.

faq.q: What if the additive comes from a premix?
faq.a: Assess its contribution, function and any carry-over conditions.

faq.q: Can one additive have different functions?
faq.a: Its label class should reflect the applicable actual function in the food.

faq.q: Are processing aids automatically omitted?
faq.a: No. Establish the relevant classification and conditions before deciding.
